why.founding: A First-Era warship from the fleet that chased Red Bramman, lost on the reef and settled upright in eleven metres.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep enough to be intact, shallow enough to dive on one breath at the stern.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody owns it; four Soulrest families dispute that.
why.pressures: Two centuries of salvage have stripped the deck; the hold is silted and nobody has cut into it.
why.wouldChangeIf: One good season of settled water would let a diving team open the hold properly.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a shipping approach or a hazard

vibe.signatureFeature: A ram-bowed hull standing upright on the bottom with its ribs open like a lantern, visible from the surface on a calm day.
vibe.palette: Green water, black timber, white sand.

places.name: Alten Meerhleel
sources: world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md (Alten Meerhleel: a port built to trade with outsiders; Hist: NONE)

why.founding: Canon's outsider-facing port north-west of Lilmoth: a working two-culture port below city scale, where an Argonian raft-quarter and an outsiders' warehouse row front the same water. With Lilmoth destroyed for a century and a half the bay's outside trade came here, and enough of it stayed that the quay outgrew the village.
why.siteAdvantages: Slow deep water inside the bar, deep enough for a laden hull to lie off and be worked by lighters, with firm enough margin behind it for a warehouse row — an *alten-* name, meaning outsiders were always the point.
why.occupantsMotive: Lightermen, Argonian raft-quarter families and factors from four ports; the customs presence is one clerk and a tariff shed nobody staffs, which is the entire commercial proposition.
why.pressures: Now that Lilmoth is rebuilt the two ports are direct rivals, and Meerhleel's whole advantage is that it asks nothing — an advantage that Corimont, the province's actual free port, holds far more securely.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Lilmoth's council ever dropped its tariffs, Meerhleel would lose the only reason anyone sails past a real harbour.

hardConstraints: sheltered navigable water off the legal lanes

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately equidistant from two customs regimes

vibe.signatureFeature: Two building grammars on one waterfront: a lashed Argonian raft-quarter and a straight-gabled outsiders' warehouse row, sharing a landing stage and no carpentry whatsoever.
vibe.palette: Sun-bleached deck timber, painted price boards, brown estuary water.
vibe.approach: From the water, masts and a warehouse gable read together before any of the rafts do.

places.reconciliationNote: Retyped from neutral-free-port (2026-09-02 reconciliation). That singular type is canon-anchored on Alten Corimont — named freehold, captain of the port, nailed price list — which keeps it; Meerhleel's canon is only 'a port built to trade with outsiders', which port-town covers honestly at the same M4 scale. ID unchanged.

why.founding: Founded on the ash-enriched firm lowland left by the Great Burn, which turned out to grow food better than the forest had.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry firm ground, deep burn ash, and the coast road for a market.
why.occupantsMotive: Mixed Argonian and Imperial-descended households farming the one soil in the district that improved.
why.pressures: The ash is finite; yields have been falling for three generations and nobody says so out loud.
why.wouldChangeIf: Exhausted soil would empty it within twenty years.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in a city's agricultural hinterland

vibe.signatureFeature: Open black-earth fields with charcoal still turning up in every furrow, hedged with wattle against guar.
vibe.palette: Black soil, pale stubble gold, green hedge.

why.founding: A village-kept fire and dry floor on the road, maintained by rota because the coast road kills people who are caught out.
why.siteAdvantages: At the point where the road leaves firm ground for the salt marsh.
why.occupantsMotive: Ashfield's households keep it in turn; using it obliges you to leave fuel.
why.pressures: Travellers routinely take fuel without leaving any, and the rota is quietly failing.
why.wouldChangeIf: A season of unkept fires would end a two-hundred-year custom.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities

vibe.signatureFeature: A single shuttered room with a banked fire, a fuel stack, and a tally board of who last filled it.
vibe.palette: Ember orange, reed brown.

why.founding: The nearest Hist village to Soulrest, and the reason the burn country still has Argonians in it at all.
why.siteAdvantages: A rise that the peat fire went around, with its tree's roots reaching water the burn never reached.
why.occupantsMotive: They kept the tree alive through the Burn and consider that the defining fact of their village.
why.pressures: Soulrest's four claimants all court them, and the village has learned to answer all four the same way.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the tree would disperse the village into the city within a generation.

hardConstraints: channel bank or spring, always with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage

vibe.signatureFeature: A blue-flowering Hist standing alone in a district of dead white stumps, ringed by a low water channel dug to keep fire out.
vibe.palette: Blue-white blossom, black ash, green channel.

why.founding: A village whose Hist died with its mnemic egg unrecovered, and which has organised its entire remaining life around that fact.
why.siteAdvantages: Unchanged good ground — they stayed, which is the unusual decision.
why.occupantsMotive: They keep the empty enclosure, keep the offices, and keep telling the memories aloud because there is nothing left to hold them.
why.pressures: The children are leaving for Lilmoth; the recitation takes six days and fewer people can do it each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: A recovered egg would restore the village at a stroke, and every treasure-hunter in Murkmire knows that.

preferences.neighbourRelation: neighbours argue about taking them in

vibe.signatureFeature: An empty walled tree-enclosure with a recitation bench facing it, worn smooth, and the whole village's memory being spoken to a stump-socket every evening.
vibe.palette: Wall moss, bare earth circle, lamp gold.

why.founding: A grave-stake field where somebody pulled the stakes, and the bog blight that canon promises duly came up.
why.siteAdvantages: An old village burial ground on soft peat — the exact condition the blight needs.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing living. The blight keeps to the field and the field is fenced by common consent.
why.pressures: The pulled stakes are still lying where they were dropped, each one a whole life's story nobody can now read back.
why.wouldChangeIf: Re-staking the field correctly would end it, and requires a grave-singer willing to walk in.

preferences.neighbourRelation: at or beside a grave-stake field

vibe.signatureFeature: A field of fallen grave-stakes lying like scattered kindling, and ground that moves slightly where nothing is walking.
vibe.palette: Peat black, bleached stake, sick green.

why.founding: Argonians who die in stone prisons can still return if their bones are brought to the dirt; somebody had to build the halfway house.
why.siteAdvantages: On the burn-country track between White Rose and the coast road, one day's carry from either.
why.occupantsMotive: Carriers rest, re-wrap and re-label here; the keeper records every name that passes through and where it is going.
why.pressures: The register is longer than the number of bodies that have actually reached a Hist.
why.wouldChangeIf: If White Rose were emptied the house would become a memorial rather than a service.

hardConstraints: on a walked or poled route

preferences.neighbourRelation: between a carceral site and the interior

vibe.signatureFeature: A low open-sided hall of racks, each rack holding a wrapped bundle with a written name and a destination village.
vibe.palette: Reed brown, bleached cloth, lamp-black ink.

why.founding: The coast road crosses the river south of Soulrest where it is too deep to ford and too wide to bridge cheaply.
why.siteAdvantages: A narrows with firm banks on both sides and slack water for an hour either side of the turn.
why.occupantsMotive: The ferry family also hire out as guides upriver, which is the more profitable half of the business.
why.pressures: Guides are hired to go upriver far more often than the traffic justifies, and the family does not discuss where.
why.wouldChangeIf: A bridge here would end both trades and has been proposed three times.

hardConstraints: across water too deep or wide to ford

preferences.neighbourRelation: a mandatory node in the route graph; has a paired stage

vibe.signatureFeature: A rope-guided flat punt and a hiring board listing upriver reaches by hours rather than by name.
vibe.palette: River brown, rope grey, green bank.

why.founding: The seaward mouth of the narrow winding river Red Bramman escaped the Alessian navy through, encased in dense mangrove.
why.siteAdvantages: Four channel mouths open off the same bay; only one carries water at the top of the tide, and only for about ninety minutes.
why.occupantsMotive: The pilots who know the run sell the knowledge and never write it down; a wrong channel strands a hull until the next tide.
why.pressures: It is a hidden route, not a scheduled lane — placing a marked ferry service on it would destroy the thing that makes it worth anything.
why.wouldChangeIf: A silt pulse could close it, or open a second, and the pilots' monopoly would end with it.

hardConstraints: tidal; passable only at low water

preferences.neighbourRelation: a shortcut that halves a journey, on a schedule

vibe.signatureFeature: Four identical mangrove mouths, one of them false-bottomed with a sand sill, and a tide-mark cut into a root that only reads at slack water.
vibe.palette: Black water, root brown, green tunnel light.
vibe.approach: From the bay it looks like solid mangrove until the tide is exactly right.

why.founding: Canon's hospitable, artisan, alliance-brokering tribe, on the cliffs above Oliis Bay — the village that knits the region back together after each catastrophe.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock bench above the bay with a single stair to a beach landing: defensible, dry, and commanding the whole approach to Lilmoth.
why.occupantsMotive: Diplomacy and craft. Their Listening-Tree and its chimes are why other tribes come to them rather than the reverse.
why.pressures: Everyone in Murkmire wants Bright-Throat's endorsement, which makes neutrality expensive to maintain.
why.wouldChangeIf: Taking a side in the Lilmoth–An-Xileel quarrel would cost them the role they are famous for.

preferences.neighbourRelation: commands a channel or a bay

vibe.signatureFeature: Houses on a cliff bench hung with tuned bone and tin chimes, so that the wind announces the village before you see it.
vibe.palette: Warm rock ochre, painted chime frames, blue bay below.
vibe.approach: Audible from the water long before it is visible — the province's one genuinely acoustic landmark.

why.founding: The dead of the Great Burn's western end, buried where they were found because there were too many to carry.
why.siteAdvantages: A rise at the edge of the ash plain, the first ground that did not burn.
why.occupantsMotive: Grave-singers still come; the count is kept and recited, and it is not a round number.
why.pressures: The stakes will not hold in ash, so the dead here are marked in stone — an admitted, resented compromise.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing changes here. That is the point of it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village

vibe.signatureFeature: Two hundred low stone cairns in rows on the edge of an ash plain, each with a grave-stake laid flat on top rather than driven in.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, white ash, one green tree.

why.founding: Two great trees' roots and branches meet forty feet above a channel too dangerous to swim, and the crossing was obvious.
why.siteAdvantages: The only place in six kilometres where the canopy actually touches across the channel.
why.occupantsMotive: Maintained by both banks' villages with lashings renewed every dry season.
why.pressures: The channel below holds the crocodile stock that makes the crossing necessary.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing either tree would end the crossing and add a day to every journey between the banks.

preferences.neighbourRelation: a shortcut between two routes

vibe.signatureFeature: A living root-and-branch bridge with lashed handlines, forty feet above water that is visibly occupied.
vibe.palette: Green canopy, pale lashing, dark water below.

why.founding: Imperial road stage east of Soulrest, canon-named as its neighbour; the Legion built it, the wreck-salvage families kept it.
why.siteAdvantages: Last firm ground before the coast road turns inland; a shingle beach below that catches everything the Southern Sea loses.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvage rights are hereditary here and jealously counted; the stage's stable block is now a drying shed for recovered cordage.
why.pressures: No stage-keeper has been paid in two centuries; the roof is Argonian thatch on Imperial walls.
why.wouldChangeIf: A revived coast road under a real toll authority would make it a proper town again.

preferences.neighbourRelation: day-travel spacing along a road

vibe.signatureFeature: An Imperial way-station wearing a reed roof, its yard stacked with ships' timber that never came from any local tree.
vibe.palette: Grey plaster, red pantile fragments, bleached driftwood.

why.founding: Bright-Throat's chime craft turned into infrastructure: a line of tuned frames along the bay that carries short messages faster than any boat.
why.siteAdvantages: Sited on the ridge and headland points where the wind is reliable and the next frame is audible.
why.occupantsMotive: Keepers are paid by Lilmoth's council and by Bright-Throat jointly, which is the only thing those two jointly do.
why.pressures: The code is limited to about forty phrases and everyone has learned to hear it, which makes privacy impossible.
why.wouldChangeIf: A silent season — no wind, or a broken frame — leaves the bay's whole warning system deaf.

preferences.neighbourRelation: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay

vibe.signatureFeature: A tall tuned bone-and-tin chime frame on a headland, with the next one just visible and always audible on the right wind.
vibe.palette: Bone white, tin grey, sky.

why.founding: An exile from Ashfield who took the ash plain because nobody follows anyone into it.
why.siteAdvantages: A void in the ash crust roofed over — warm, dry, and effectively invisible.
why.occupantsMotive: Wants to be left alone; will trade knowledge of where the ground is safe for food.
why.pressures: The ground under the hut is not stable and the hermit knows it better than anyone.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would kill them, and the district would lose its only map of the voids.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately far from everything; the effort-to-reach IS the design

vibe.signatureFeature: A roof at ground level over a burnt-out peat void, with cane markers stuck across the plain in a pattern only one person can read.
vibe.palette: Ash grey, cane pale, single fire-glow.

why.founding: Canon puts the Great Burn's underground peat network running from Stormhold to Soulrest; this village sat on top of it when the ground caught.
why.siteAdvantages: It was a good dry rise. It was dry because there was burning peat under it.
why.occupantsMotive: A handful of caretaker families live at the edge and keep the hearths cold as a matter of principle.
why.pressures: The peat is still smouldering somewhere under the district and nobody knows where it will surface.
why.wouldChangeIf: A new vent under the caretakers' hamlet would move them permanently.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in the burn country of the west

vibe.signatureFeature: House platforms standing over a collapsed, still-warm ground surface, with smoke rising from a crack half a mile away.
vibe.palette: Ash grey, ember orange at night, dead white stumps.

why.founding: The unlicensed version of the same trade, working a xanmeer that has no tending clan left to object.
why.siteAdvantages: Two hours off the nearest channel, screened, and reachable only by a route the crew cut themselves.
why.occupantsMotive: They are being paid by lot, not by wage, by a buyer none of them has met.
why.pressures: They have hit something with a live mechanism and have not told the buyer.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single fatality would scatter the crew and leave the cut open.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor, or at an unwatched ruin

vibe.signatureFeature: A spoil heap hidden under cut vegetation, a shored shaft, and a crate of finds already packed with a Lilmoth shipping mark on it.
vibe.palette: Wet spoil black, lamp yellow, green cover.

why.founding: A rest house on the coast road kept for travelling Nisswo, because the road between Soulrest and the interior has nothing else on it.
why.siteAdvantages: Half a day from either end of an empty stretch, on the dry side of the road, with its own well.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper feeds anyone and preaches at everyone; both are non-negotiable.
why.pressures: Travellers who want a bed without a sermon walk on and sleep badly.
why.wouldChangeIf: A second rest house nearby would empty it instantly, and the keeper knows it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: between villages on a preaching circuit

vibe.signatureFeature: A single long room with the road running past its open front and the preaching bench set where you cannot avoid it.
vibe.palette: Reed brown, lamp yellow, black doorway.

why.founding: An Imperial road stage counted from Soulrest, still called by its number two centuries after the count stopped mattering.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry rise with a well, at an Imperial day's march from the last one.
why.occupantsMotive: An Argonian family keeps it and rebuilt the roof in reed; they still use the Imperial numbering.
why.pressures: The well is the only good water for six miles and everyone knows it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A failed well would end the stage and shift the road's rhythm entirely.

preferences.neighbourRelation: day-travel spacing; something named within 300 m of the road

vibe.signatureFeature: An Imperial milestone with its number recut by hand, standing outside a reed-roofed stone shell.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, reed gold, dust.

why.founding: The only roofed building on the long empty stretch of the coast road east of Soulrest.
why.siteAdvantages: Exactly half a day's walk from each end, on the first dry ground past the salt marsh.
why.occupantsMotive: It exists because the alternative is sleeping in the marsh, and it prices accordingly.
why.pressures: Bandit-adjacent salvage families use it as a meeting room and the keeper does not object.
why.wouldChangeIf: A second stage house would halve its trade and its usefulness.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement

vibe.signatureFeature: One long low room with the road's mud tracked to the doorway and a strongbox chained to the hearth.
vibe.palette: Smoke brown, mud, firelight.

why.founding: An Imperial stone arch on the coast road that a local family has been collecting on since the Legion stopped.
why.siteAdvantages: The one crossing of a tidal creek that does not require a boat within four miles.
why.occupantsMotive: The toll is small, consistent and entirely without legal basis; it buys maintenance that genuinely happens.
why.pressures: Soulrest's council would like the revenue and has no way to take it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapsed arch would end the family, the toll and the road in one night.

hardConstraints: spans a channel at its narrowest

preferences.neighbourRelation: on the route graph; its owner lives within sight

vibe.signatureFeature: A single Imperial arch in perfect repair with an Argonian toll shelter built onto its parapet.
vibe.palette: Grey ashlar, reed roof, tidal brown.

why.founding: Imperial harbour works lit the Topal approach for four centuries; the oil contract ended with the province.
why.siteAdvantages: The highest headland on the bay approach, and one of the few structures in the province that breaks the canopy line.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. A Soulrest chandler still bills the council for lamp oil that is never delivered.
why.pressures: The lantern glass is gone; the stair is sound; whoever relights it decides who profits from the bar.
why.wouldChangeIf: Relighting it kills the Long Bar and makes Soulrest's harbour honest.

preferences.neighbourRelation: one per hazardous approach

vibe.signatureFeature: A squat Imperial tower with a dead lantern room, the only long sightline on the whole south-west coast.
vibe.palette: Lime render gone green, rust streaks, black basalt plinth.

why.founding: Cyrodilic Collections' Lilmoth store: the antiquities they shipped out, and the ones they never got permission to.
why.siteAdvantages: One of the intact Imperial buildings near the wall, dry and defensible, with a water gate for crates.
why.occupantsMotive: A resident agent, two guards, and a catalogue that does not match the shelves.
why.pressures: Half the tribes of Murkmire have a claim on something in here and Collections knows the list.
why.wouldChangeIf: A repatriation ruling by the council would empty it and set a precedent across the province.

preferences.neighbourRelation: attached to a port or a wharf

vibe.signatureFeature: Imperial vaulted storerooms of crated antiquities, each crate stencilled with a find-site the local villages can read.
vibe.palette: Crate pine, brass seal, lamp shadow.

why.founding: Cyrodilic Collections' forward station for the Murkmire xanmeer survey — a foreign presence Argonians can argue with rather than fight.
why.siteAdvantages: Central to four xanmeers, on firm ground with a boat landing and a defensible single approach.
why.occupantsMotive: Surveyors, a local guide contingent who set most of the actual rules, and a permanent argument about what may be lifted.
why.pressures: The guides have veto in practice and no veto on paper, and the paper is starting to matter.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single unauthorised lift would end the guides' cooperation and the station with it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately near something interesting and far from help

vibe.signatureFeature: A stilted survey hut with a drafting table under a canvas fly, and a rack of numbered finds that the guides count every evening.
vibe.palette: Canvas cream, drawing ink, green shade.

why.founding: Crocodiles are farmed here for hide, meat and — chiefly — for sale to villages that want a defended water approach.
why.siteAdvantages: A creek that can be gated at both ends, with tidal flushing that keeps the pens clean.
why.occupantsMotive: Breeding stock is the valuable part; a village that buys a pair has bought a wall.
why.pressures: Escapes are frequent, deniable and very bad for the neighbours.
why.wouldChangeIf: An escape into Lilmoth's approach channels would end the trade by decree.

preferences.neighbourRelation: attached to a village or a city canal system

vibe.signatureFeature: A gated creek divided into numbered pens by stake fences, with feeding platforms above each and no railing anywhere.
vibe.palette: Brown water, grey hide, bleached stake.

why.founding: A herd of water-adapted guar is pastured on submerged weed meadows, and the byre had to go where the fodder is.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow weed flat in two metres of clear water with a firm bottom the animals can stand on.
why.occupantsMotive: The herders swim their rounds; the stock is worth more than any dry-land herd in the district and eats free.
why.pressures: A ripper-eel getting into the flat costs a season's calves.
why.wouldChangeIf: Silting the flat would kill the weed and the whole practice.

preferences.neighbourRelation: serves a coastal settlement's transport

vibe.signatureFeature: Feeding racks and a stock pen standing in open water, with the herd's backs breaking the surface as they graze the bottom.
vibe.palette: Clear green water, pale weed, wet grey hide.

why.founding: A camp working the wamasu and crocodile nesting grounds for eggs, which are worth more than the animals.
why.siteAdvantages: Between three nesting grounds, screened, with a fast water route out to Alten Meerhleel.
why.occupantsMotive: Egg money is very good and the risk is entirely from the animals, not from any law.
why.pressures: Taking wamasu eggs brings the adult, and the adult curses the water for a hundred paces.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single wamasu following them home would end the camp.

preferences.neighbourRelation: just outside a village's watched ground

vibe.signatureFeature: A camp of packed straw crates under netting, with three different species' eggs sorted by size and a very careful fire.
vibe.palette: Straw gold, netting grey, green shade.

why.founding: Built for the Expeditionary Force canon says was sent to quell the 3E 427 uprisings; abandoned when the province was lost six years later.
why.siteAdvantages: On the rise commanding the road from the plantations to the port — the line the uprising used.
why.occupantsMotive: Collapsed and roofless; a poacher crew winters in the gatehouse.
why.pressures: Its armoury was emptied by the tribes, and some of what came out is still in circulation.
why.wouldChangeIf: A faction refortifying it would immediately be a regional power.

hardConstraints: commands something that no longer matters

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a dead road

vibe.signatureFeature: A collapsed Legion fort whose walls are down but whose gatehouse still stands with the eagle uncut above the arch.
vibe.palette: Rubble grey, thorn green, rust.

why.founding: Two villages' worth of households whose ground flooded permanently three seasons ago and who have not been resettled.
why.siteAdvantages: The nearest dry rise to their lost fields, and within reach of the fair.
why.occupantsMotive: They intend to go back; the water does not intend to leave.
why.pressures: Soulrest will not grant land; the villages inland will not absorb them; the camp is becoming permanent architecture.
why.wouldChangeIf: A land grant would turn it into a village overnight, which is exactly why it has not been granted.

hardConstraints: wherever they were allowed to stop

preferences.neighbourRelation: just outside a settlement that has not taken them in

vibe.signatureFeature: Shelters that started as tents and have grown plank walls, arranged in two distinct village layouts side by side.
vibe.palette: Tarpaulin grey, salvaged plank, mud.

why.founding: A village that keeps gar the way other villages keep guar: penned, bred, and used to clear channels of anything else.
why.siteAdvantages: A network of gateable channels with reliable flow, which is what gar-keeping requires and almost nowhere has.
why.occupantsMotive: A gar-cleared channel is a safe channel, and villages pay for the service — the fish are the by-product.
why.pressures: A gar loose in a paddy is a catastrophe, and one got out three seasons ago.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single loss of control would end the trade and the village's welcome everywhere.

hardConstraints: penned water separated from open channel

preferences.neighbourRelation: supplies mounts or protection to a district

vibe.signatureFeature: A village whose streets are gated water channels, with a keeper's pole and a counting board at every gate.
vibe.palette: Dark water, pale gate timber, silver fish.

why.founding: A still fen where the water plants light from below all year, which is why the pilgrim route runs through it at night.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow, warm, flow-free basin — the conditions the glow needs, and rare.
why.occupantsMotive: Gatherers take the plants for lamp-jelly; pilgrims cross at night because the fen lights the way.
why.pressures: Harvesting dims it; the villages ration the take by an argument nobody enjoys having.
why.wouldChangeIf: Over-harvest would end both the trade and the route in the same season.

preferences.neighbourRelation: known and visited; a destination, not a secret

vibe.signatureFeature: Standing water lit green-blue from beneath, so that poling canoes throw shadows upward onto the canopy.
vibe.palette: Green-blue glow, black canopy, silhouettes.

why.founding: Canon names gold as one of Soulrest's two exports and says the tribes halted it in 3E 427; this is where it came out of the ground.
why.siteAdvantages: A quartz reef in the low hills behind the burn country, close enough to barge ore down to the port.
why.occupantsMotive: Empty of workers. A survey office, a stamping floor and three adits that still run wet.
why.pressures: There is gold left. Everyone knows there is gold left. Nobody local will be the one to reopen it.
why.wouldChangeIf: An outside company with its own guards would restart the whole 3E 427 argument.

preferences.neighbourRelation: behind a coastal ex-capital, on a dead haul road

vibe.signatureFeature: A stamping floor with its timbers standing and its iron gone, and three adit mouths breathing cold air into a hot forest.
vibe.palette: Quartz white, rust, deep shade green.

why.founding: A guides' camp on the jungle route north of Lilmoth, kept because parties that cross without a guide do not always arrive.
why.siteAdvantages: A defensible island of firm ground at the halfway point of a two-day crossing.
why.occupantsMotive: Guides sell the crossing, not the camp; the camp exists so that they survive selling it.
why.pressures: The route's danger has risen since the eastern causeway failed and traffic was pushed onto this line.
why.wouldChangeIf: A repaired causeway would empty this camp and this route entirely.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a guided route, day-travel spacing

vibe.signatureFeature: A ring of thorn and a raised sleeping platform above head height, with fire pits placed to light the approaches rather than the camp.
vibe.palette: Thorn grey, fire orange, black jungle.

why.founding: Haj-mota shell is the province's best shield and roof material, and Lilmoth is where it is worked at scale.
why.siteAdvantages: On the shore road with a boiling pit, a soaking tank and the strand within a morning's haul.
why.occupantsMotive: Shell is bought by weight and sold by curve; the yard's whole skill is in knowing which plate becomes what.
why.pressures: Supply depends on a moult season nobody controls; two thin years would close the yard.
why.wouldChangeIf: A shift in the basking ground would move the entire trade east.

preferences.neighbourRelation: supplies a village's defence

vibe.signatureFeature: Stacked curved shell plates sorted by size against a wall, with a soaking tank of black liquor and a shieldwright's bench under the same roof.
vibe.palette: Shell brown-grey, black liquor, bone white.

why.founding: A raised hammock's crown given over entirely to the ancestors of the villages around it — the only ground high enough to stay dry in any flood.
why.siteAdvantages: The highest dry ground in a wide floodplain, which makes it the only permanent burial terrace available.
why.occupantsMotive: Four villages bury here in four sectors, and the sector boundaries are the oldest agreed lines in the district.
why.pressures: The hammock is running out of terrace and no village will yield an inch of its sector.
why.wouldChangeIf: A flood high enough to reach the crown would be read as a judgement on all four.

hardConstraints: above the flood on a tree-island

preferences.neighbourRelation: one per inhabited hammock; the region's signature sacred form

vibe.signatureFeature: A tree-crowned rise terraced into four quarters by low stone kerbs, each quarter's stakes carved in a different village's hand.
vibe.palette: Green crown, pale stake, brown flood plain below.

why.founding: A village on a tree-island hammock, reached only by water, with its fields on smaller hammocks around it.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry wooded island in permanent marsh, with a ring of satellite hammocks at poling distance.
why.occupantsMotive: Island living gives them the safest ground in the district and the longest journey to market, and they have chosen the former for centuries.
why.pressures: Every child leaves for Lilmoth for a season; roughly half return, and the number is falling.
why.wouldChangeIf: A poling route improvement would connect them to the city and change everything about them.

preferences.neighbourRelation: a local centre; neighbours come here in flood

vibe.signatureFeature: A village entirely under old canopy on an island, with its canoe fleet drawn up in a single beach notch and its fields visible as green dots across open water.
vibe.palette: Deep canopy shade, water silver, thatch.

why.founding: Canon puts a river starting just south of Soulrest and running north-east into the interior; this is the last point a sea-going hull can reach on it.
why.siteAdvantages: A gravel sill across the channel: deep water below it, poling water above it, and firm banks for transhipment.
why.occupantsMotive: Everything going inland is broken down into canoe loads here, by people who charge for it.
why.pressures: Whoever controls this sill controls the whole interior trade of the south-west, and four parties know that.
why.wouldChangeIf: Dredging the sill would destroy the transhipment trade and enrich the city.

preferences.neighbourRelation: the hinge between a boat lane and a land route; a mandatory node

vibe.signatureFeature: Sea hulls tied nose-to-tail below a gravel bar and a hundred canoes drawn up above it, with a portage yard between.
vibe.palette: Gravel grey, hull tar, cane green.

why.founding: The engineered half of Hereguard: sluices, bunds and a controlled flood cycle, which is the only Imperial-era engineering in Murkmire still doing its job.
why.siteAdvantages: A gradient gentle enough to terrace and a river reliable enough to flood on schedule.
why.occupantsMotive: Water is allocated by a rota that is the single most argued-about document in the district.
why.pressures: One tenant taking water out of turn ruins a terrace three levels down.
why.wouldChangeIf: A bund failure in the wet season would take the whole staircase in one night.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in a city's hinterland; owned

vibe.signatureFeature: A mile-long staircase of water, each level a different green, with plank walkways along every bund.
vibe.palette: Mirror silver, shoot green, mud brown.

why.founding: Canon's rice estate north of Lilmoth and one of the few places Bretons still live in Argonia; rice is the one crop that works here because it wants the flood.
why.siteAdvantages: A flooding river terrace that ruins any other crop and suits this one exactly.
why.occupantsMotive: A Breton family and Argonian tenant households, bound by a share arrangement that both sides describe differently.
why.pressures: Lilmoth depends on Hereguard rice, which gives the tenants more leverage every year and the family less.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tenant refusal at planting would starve the city, and everyone has done that arithmetic.

hardConstraints: controls a crossing or a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: holds the crossing its neighbours must use

vibe.signatureFeature: A Breton stone house with a tiled roof standing at the head of a mile of terraced rice paddy worked entirely in Argonian fashion.
vibe.palette: Water-mirror paddy, green shoots, grey Breton slate.

why.founding: Raised for the Alessian sailors lost hunting Red Bramman, on the headland from which the fleet entered the river.
why.siteAdvantages: On the headland above Bramman's mouth, facing water it cannot see into.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody tends it; the pilots of Screen-Watch consider it a useful navigation mark and nothing else.
why.pressures: The inscription names the river, which is the single most useful piece of public information about a hidden route.
why.wouldChangeIf: Someone defacing the river's name would be an act of policy.

preferences.neighbourRelation: at or overlooking the event's site

vibe.signatureFeature: A weathered Imperial pillar whose worn inscription is still the only written record that names Bramman's river.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, orange lichen, green scrub.

why.founding: The shortest line between the Topal headlands, named for the Empress whose navy hunted Red Bramman down it.
why.siteAdvantages: A wind shadow behind the high islands where a sailing hull loses way for an hour every afternoon.
why.occupantsMotive: Khajiit and Argonian crews who row, not sail, and therefore choose exactly when the lane is used.
why.pressures: Everyone knows about the lane; captains still take it because going around costs a day.
why.wouldChangeIf: A patrolled escort schedule out of Soulrest would price the risk away.

hardConstraints: on the shipping lane, sheltered from wind

preferences.neighbourRelation: on the Archon-Lilmoth-Soulrest-Tear line

vibe.signatureFeature: Glassy water with sails hanging slack, and low rowed craft appearing from the island shadow.
vibe.palette: Mirror-flat pewter, black island silhouettes.

why.founding: Where four elevated walkways meet above the mangrove, a platform grew that is now a place in its own right.
why.siteAdvantages: The one point at which the whole upper network of this district connects, twelve metres above the water.
why.occupantsMotive: A tea-seller, a chime-relay peg board and a toll nobody formally imposes but everybody pays.
why.pressures: The junction's timbers carry more traffic than they were built for and everybody can feel it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would sever the district's upper network into four dead ends.

preferences.neighbourRelation: connects three or more water settlements

vibe.signatureFeature: A crossing platform high in the canopy with four decks radiating from it and a rope-lift shaft dropping to the water.
vibe.palette: Canopy green, sun shafts, worn deck grey.

why.founding: Lilmoth has a Hist but no native tribe, and a fourth of the people who arrive here have no tree at all; the Fringe is where they end up.
why.siteAdvantages: Just outside the wall on ground the city does not tax and the villages will not claim.
why.occupantsMotive: Mutual aid without kinship — the households here are organised by arrival date, not by clan.
why.pressures: Hissmir is two provinces away in practical terms; most people here will never make the pilgrimage and know it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A city grant of tree-access would empty half of it in a month.

hardConstraints: wherever they were allowed to stop

preferences.neighbourRelation: on the edge of somewhere that would not take them in

vibe.signatureFeature: A quarter with no village-tree at its centre and a bare swept circle where one would be, kept clear on purpose.
vibe.palette: Dun mud-plaster, patched cloth, an empty green circle.

why.founding: A village founded around a cutting taken after Umbriel, by households from three stripped villages who had nothing else in common.
why.siteAdvantages: A raised hammock above the flood with good drainage — chosen for the cutting's sake, not the people's.
why.occupantsMotive: Everything here is a hundred and fifty years old at most, including the customs, and they know it.
why.pressures: The cutting is still young; if it fails, three villages' worth of memory fails with it.
why.wouldChangeIf: The tree reaching maturity would settle the village's status and end an argument with its neighbours about precedence.

hardConstraints: channel bank or spring, always with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage

vibe.signatureFeature: A young Hist barely thicker than a person, inside a stockade far larger than it needs, built for the tree it will become.
vibe.palette: Pale young bark, new timber, bright green.

why.founding: A Murkmire village whose tree speaks clearly and often, which makes it the region's arbiter whether it wants to be or not.
why.siteAdvantages: A river terrace on the Keel-Sakka with deep root-water and a defensible bend.
why.occupantsMotive: Their tree-minder is consulted from three days' travel away, which is a burden the village debates constantly.
why.pressures: Lilmoth's tree does not speak to anyone but its minders; this one speaks to everybody, and the comparison is politically loaded.
why.wouldChangeIf: If their tree fell silent the region would lose its only uncontested voice.

hardConstraints: channel bank or spring, always with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage

vibe.signatureFeature: A village built as a ring facing inward at its tree, with a speaking-floor of laid planks worn white by generations of listeners.
vibe.palette: Deep green canopy, pale plank, red-brown thatch.

why.founding: A merchantman driven ashore in a storm and never refloated; the village that gathered around it roofed it instead.
why.siteAdvantages: High on the strand above the tide, with a whole hull's worth of dry seasoned timber already in place.
why.occupantsMotive: A shore family who charge for a dry night and sell salvaged fittings out of the stern.
why.pressures: The hull is two hundred years old and the keel is going; the roof is reed and the walls are ship.
why.wouldChangeIf: When the keel finally breaks, the hall becomes a boat-shaped ruin and the family moves inland.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a shipping approach or a hazard

vibe.signatureFeature: An upturned hull as a longhouse, with the sternpost carved into a door frame and the gunports as windows.
vibe.palette: Silvered oak, reed gold, sand.

why.founding: An unlicensed sap camp working a wild Hist-kin stand well inside the jungle belt, where nobody with authority goes.
why.siteAdvantages: Four hours from any village, on a stand nobody has claimed, with water to move the barrels out.
why.occupantsMotive: Sap sells for more in Lilmoth than anything else the jungle produces, and the buyers do not ask.
why.pressures: The tappers are not Argonian-local and do not know what they are doing to the stand.
why.wouldChangeIf: Discovery by any village tree-minder would end it violently.

preferences.neighbourRelation: at an isolated or rogue Hist, far from a village

vibe.signatureFeature: Tapped trunks with crude iron spiles and stacked barrels under a leaf roof, in a stand where every other tree is untouched.
vibe.palette: Amber sap, iron black, deep green.

why.founding: A tribe that never left its xanmeer, and therefore holds the strongest fortification in southern Murkmire without having built anything.
why.siteAdvantages: Stone walls, a single water approach, and ancient defences that still work — in a region where everything else is timber.
why.occupantsMotive: They are polite, immovable, and entirely uninterested in Lilmoth's politics or the An-Xileel's.
why.pressures: Every faction in the south has wanted their walls at some point; the working defences are why none has taken them.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the vakka mechanisms ever failed, the village would be ordinary overnight.

preferences.neighbourRelation: dominates its immediate district

vibe.signatureFeature: A living village on the terraces of a stepped stone pyramid, with washing lines between carved lintels and a discharge-scarred approach causeway.
vibe.palette: Warm grey stone, bright cloth, black scorch marks.
vibe.approach: The only stone silhouette in the district; it reads above the canopy from two directions.

why.founding: A village in the jungle belt that has refused every outside contact since 4E 48 and enforces the refusal at the boundary.
why.siteAdvantages: A defensible rise with one approach, three days from Lilmoth and unreachable by water.
why.occupantsMotive: They lost a village to something that came from outside and have drawn the obvious conclusion.
why.pressures: Their boundary now crosses a route the guides need, and the guides have started going around.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single successful parley would open the shortest route across the belt.

hardConstraints: defensible approach, often a single crossing

preferences.neighbourRelation: has an enemy; the enemy's ground is nearby

vibe.signatureFeature: A totem boundary line with fresh offerings and fresh spear-marks on the same posts, and no path beyond it.
vibe.palette: Ochre totem paint, deep green, dark timber.

why.founding: The xanmeer the An-Xileel pumped out room by room and held dry with magicks; with them gone the magicks lapsed and the silt returned.
why.siteAdvantages: Sits in standing water west of Lilmoth; only the topmost chamber stands above the silt, exactly as canon first found it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody tends it. Divers go in for what the An-Xileel left behind when the water came back fast.
why.pressures: The lower rooms are silt, not water — a diver can enter them and not find the way out.
why.wouldChangeIf: Another pumping effort would reopen it, and there is no faction left with the will or the singing to do it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in drowned country; often near a drowned village

vibe.signatureFeature: One stone chamber standing clear of flat water, with the pumping gear of a fanatical state party still bolted to its lintel and rusting.
vibe.palette: Grey silt water, wet stone, orange rust.
vibe.approach: A single square of masonry in an otherwise empty sheet of water.

why.founding: The Keel-Sakka drops nine metres over a rock lip, and has cut a chamber behind the fall.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry chamber behind falling water: hidden, cool and audible from half a kilometre.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody permanently. It has been a shrine, a cache and a hiding place in that order and probably again.
why.pressures: The chamber floods when the river rises, which is roughly when people most want to hide in it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A change in the river's course would empty and expose it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a river with real relief — the rim and upland only

vibe.signatureFeature: A curtain of water with a dry room behind it, its back wall covered in overlapping marks left by everyone who ever sheltered there.
vibe.palette: White water, black wet rock, green light.

why.founding: The furthest point a loaded canoe can reach up the Keel-Sakka, and only in the wet season; in the dry it is two kilometres downstream.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock sill that is a rapid in the wet and a dry step in the dry, with a level bank for stacking cargo.
why.occupantsMotive: Porters take over here, and their season is defined entirely by where the head of navigation is this month.
why.pressures: The moving head means the porter yard is rebuilt twice a year and nobody will build anything permanent.
why.wouldChangeIf: Cutting the sill would push navigation four kilometres further in and destroy the porters' trade.

preferences.neighbourRelation: the hinge between a boat lane and a land route; a mandatory node

vibe.signatureFeature: A stacking bank with two abandoned upstream yards visible from it, marking where the head of navigation stood in wetter years.
vibe.palette: Wet rock, stacked crate, brown flood water.

why.founding: The first village up the Keel-Sakka river from Lilmoth, where the rainforest road meets poling water.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm channel edge with deep water alongside, on the road out of Lilmoth's north gate.
why.occupantsMotive: They take Lilmoth's freight off the road and put it on the river, and charge for the change of medium.
why.pressures: Bright-Throat's chime-relay reaches here and Lilmoth's writ does not, which suits everyone locally.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cart road up the river would end the village's whole function.

hardConstraints: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed

preferences.neighbourRelation: strung along a waterway, linear not radial

vibe.signatureFeature: A single line of stilt houses along one bank with a continuous loading deck under them and canoes racked overhead.
vibe.palette: Green river, pale deck timber, red-brown thatch.

why.founding: A grove kept for Keshu the Black Fin, Murkmire's national hero — a hero-Hist grove is what a village does with a person it cannot let go of.
why.siteAdvantages: A stand of old Hist-kin trees on the ground where the story says she mustered, with a spring at the centre.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by rota from four villages, none of which will concede that the grove is any one of theirs.
why.pressures: The story has four incompatible versions and the rota is how the villages avoid resolving it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A definitive account would give the grove to one village and start a feud.

hardConstraints: spring or still water at the root

preferences.neighbourRelation: a regional centre; routes converge on it

vibe.signatureFeature: A grove of old trees with a muster-stone at its centre, and four separate offering-racks around it that never touch.
vibe.palette: Deep shade, moss, four different cloth colours.

heroHist.note: Register grove of hero rank, but NOT one of the ten power slots — reserve. Kept as a record and a swap candidate if the owner wants a Murkmire slot instead of one of the ten.

why.founding: Households who could not get shore rights near Soulrest built on water instead, where nobody could charge them ground rent.
why.siteAdvantages: A sheltered inner lagoon with two metres of still water and mooring posts already driven for the salt trade.
why.occupantsMotive: Rent-free living in sight of the city; the mooring fee is a fraction of a shore plot.
why.pressures: The council has twice tried to tax the moorings and twice failed to define them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A legal definition of a mooring as a dwelling would end it.

hardConstraints: floats; needs sheltered water and mooring points

preferences.neighbourRelation: has two or three fixed moorings keyed to the flood cycle

vibe.signatureFeature: Twenty platform houses moored in a loose ring, with the gaps between them used as streets by canoe.
vibe.palette: Wet timber, laundry colour, still green water.

why.founding: Canon: Lilmoth is built over shallow water and large ships cannot dock, so goods are lightered ashore — and the lighter crews live afloat, between the anchorage and the quay.
why.siteAdvantages: A permanent moored ground in the estuary, half a mile off the quay, out of the tariff line and inside the sheltered water.
why.occupantsMotive: The crews control the only link between deep-water hulls and the city, and they know precisely what that is worth.
why.pressures: A council attempt to license lightering triggered a two-week stoppage that nobody wants to repeat.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dredged deep-water channel would end both the flotilla and the city's leverage over its own trade.

hardConstraints: sheltered saltwater with a reef or bar

preferences.neighbourRelation: trades with a shore settlement it does not live in

vibe.signatureFeature: Forty working boats permanently moored as houses in a floating street, each with its cargo rig still stepped and its washing between the shrouds.
vibe.palette: Tarred hulls, bright laundry, brown estuary.
vibe.mood: Independent, unionised in all but name.

places.name: Lilmoth

why.founding: Rebuilt after the Slaughter of 4E 48 on the best natural harbour of the south coast, smaller and lower than the city it replaced.
why.siteAdvantages: A river estuary into Oliis Bay over shallow water; big hulls anchor out and lighter in, which is the whole economy.
why.occupantsMotive: A reconstituted merchant council governs by tariff; nobody wants a ruler, and the last party that had one killed the city.
why.pressures: Politically hostile to the An-Xileel successor state; commercially essential to a bay that must trade somewhere; built over its own mass grave.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the third Hist ever spoke to one faction alone, every institution here would break at once — which is why the rules forbid it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: bay port with a second door (a floating port) across the water
preferences.densityGradient: city core; the densest civil gradient in the south

vibe.signatureFeature: Ninety per cent Argonian stilt-and-platform work climbing high over drowned Imperial villas, inside a wall that is Imperial on three sides and Argonian facing the estuary.
vibe.palette: Wet grey timber, mould green, gold lamp-light in the upper walkways; below, still black water.
vibe.approach: From the bay the upper platforms read first, and the drowned quarter only when you are inside the wall.

places.complexityJustification: A major city on stilts over a drowned predecessor: two vertical layers, a walled circuit, a tended Hist and a repopulated slum. Compiled from the blueprint schema.

heroHist.note: Hero Hist 3/10. CANON_EXPLICIT: Lilmoth possesses its own Hist despite having no native tribe. This is the THIRD tree, grown after 4E 48 from a root fragment of the second. Young and watched: feared and tended anyway (hist-placement.md §4) — the minder's post rotates, a second tender is always present, and no faction may claim exclusive access.

why.founding: Livestock cannot go inside a stilt city, so the beast market is outside the north gate on the only firm ground.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry, level and fenced, with water on one side and the road on the other.
why.occupantsMotive: Guar, lizard-steeds, pen-bred crocodiles and hatchling stock, sold by tribes who will not enter the walls.
why.pressures: Half the sellers refuse city coin and the money-changers who solve that take a cut of every animal sold.
why.wouldChangeIf: A city livestock tariff would move the market to Alten Meerhleel overnight.

hardConstraints: a landing, because most goods come by water

preferences.neighbourRelation: on neutral ground between settlements, or in an M3+ settlement

vibe.signatureFeature: A stockade of numbered pens on firm ground outside a city that has no ground, loud from dawn, empty by dusk.
vibe.palette: Dust ochre, hide colours, red pen-paint.

why.founding: A city that lighters everything and poles the rest needs more canoes than any other place in the province, and builds them here.
why.siteAdvantages: On the water's edge with a steam pit, a bending frame and reed beds within poling distance.
why.occupantsMotive: Three yards' worth of families working one shore, competing on hull shape and cooperating on materials.
why.pressures: Good cane is coming from further away every year as the near beds are over-cut.
why.wouldChangeIf: A reed-bed failure would raise the price of every hull in the bay.

preferences.neighbourRelation: serves a port or a water-village cluster

vibe.signatureFeature: Rows of half-built hulls on trestles at every stage from bent frame to lacquered finish, under one continuous open roof.
vibe.palette: Pale cane, black lacquer, steam white.

why.founding: Lilmoth stands on a drowned city and salvage from underneath it is a licensed, taxed, entirely respectable trade.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay directly above the deepest of the sunken villas, with a stair down to a landing at water level.
why.occupantsMotive: Crews work the drowned quarter by permit, in pairs, and hand everything to the yard for valuation.
why.pressures: Some of what comes up belongs to families still living, and the yard has to decide that daily.
why.wouldChangeIf: A find of An-Xileel material would turn a trade into a political incident.

preferences.neighbourRelation: always paired with drowned ground it works

vibe.signatureFeature: A valuation floor of mould-blackened Imperial household goods laid out in lots, dripping, with a diving stair going straight down into the city.
vibe.palette: Black mould, tarnished silver, green water light.

why.founding: Where the merchant council's tariff is actually applied, argued and evaded, one lot at a time.
why.siteAdvantages: On the lighter quay, between the water stair and the warehouse row.
why.occupantsMotive: Council clerks, lighter captains and brokers in one room, which is deliberate.
why.pressures: Foreigners were once restricted to the docks by law; the law lapsed and the habit did not.
why.wouldChangeIf: A formal foreign quarter inside the wall would empty this room of half its business.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement

vibe.signatureFeature: A public scale under a lantern with the day's tariff chalked beside it, and three separate sets of books being kept at the same table.
vibe.palette: Brass and chalk, wet plank, lamp gold.

places.name: The Long Bar

why.founding: A shoal bar off the salvage coast where a false light has been shown for longer than anyone will admit.
why.siteAdvantages: Two miles of breaking bar on the Southern Sea approach, invisible from the coast road, hidden from Soulrest by the islands.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvage families who decided that waiting for wrecks was inefficient; they take the low-profile Southern Sea traders nobody reports missing.
why.pressures: Khajiit crews keep the same lane and have begun to notice; the Soulrest harbour office would have to act if it were ever proved.
why.wouldChangeIf: A working lighthouse on the headland would end it in one season.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a shipping approach with reefs or bars

vibe.signatureFeature: A driftwood pyre-frame on stilts above the tide line and a beach of sorted cargo laid out in lots.
vibe.palette: Black wet shingle, salt-white bone, tarred rope.
vibe.approach: Only readable at night, and then only as a light in the wrong place.

places.reconciliationNote: Contestable CONFIRMED here (2026-09-02 reconciliation). wrecker-beach belongs to the Soulrest salvage coast — canon's own economy for this stretch — and mercantile-coast is the only region file whose siting profile carries the ocean and breaking-bar landforms the type requires. No competing claim was found in any other file.

why.founding: A survivor of a stripped village who walked into the jungle in 4E 48 and never came out; a descendant is there now.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep enough that nobody arrives by accident, beside water, under permanent canopy.
why.occupantsMotive: The occupant talks continuously to somebody who is not present and has done so for their whole life.
why.pressures: What they say includes an accurate description of the Umbriel shadow track, which they cannot have witnessed.
why.wouldChangeIf: Anyone who wrote down what is said here would have the best surviving account of 4E 48.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately far from everything; the effort-to-reach IS the design

vibe.signatureFeature: A hut hung with hundreds of carved tally-sticks, and one voice audible from a hundred paces in an otherwise empty forest.
vibe.palette: Green dark, pale sticks, single fire.

why.founding: A Blackguard crew took a dead-end mangrove cut on Bramman's river as a staging point for cargo the pilots refuse to carry.
why.siteAdvantages: A blind channel with one entrance, deep enough to float a laden canoe, screened on every side.
why.occupantsMotive: They want the river to become a road with a toll on it, and they are prepared to be patient.
why.pressures: Screen-Watch will not deal with them; the Rose's ledgered crews think this lot are amateurs.
why.wouldChangeIf: A pilot family turning informer would end the crew inside a month.

preferences.neighbourRelation: answers to a reoccupied prison

vibe.signatureFeature: Netting slung between mangroves over a canoe berth, and a stack of unlabelled crates keeping dry on a root platform.
vibe.palette: Wet black, tarpaulin grey, weapon-steel.

why.founding: A miregaunt keeps the approach to a xanmeer nobody has entered in living memory, and has done since before anyone measured.
why.siteAdvantages: The single dry approach to the ruin; there is no way round it that is not swimming.
why.occupantsMotive: It is part of the land. It does not pursue, it does not negotiate, and it comes back.
why.pressures: Whatever it is protecting or imprisoning is inside, and that is the only argument for going past it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing changes it. Killing it changes nothing.

preferences.neighbourRelation: between a route and something worth reaching

vibe.signatureFeature: A causeway approach with a single standing shape at its midpoint that has been described identically by witnesses two centuries apart.
vibe.palette: Grey-green, moss, standing water.

why.founding: One of the plantations canon says the tribes destroyed in the 3E 427 uprisings, burned with its exports still in the yard.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm lowland with river access to Soulrest — the reason it was worth burning.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody has reoccupied the great house; the quarters behind it were dismantled for materials within a year.
why.pressures: The families who burned it live four miles away and have never once denied it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A claimant with an Imperial deed and armed help could reopen the whole grievance.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in the ex-Imperial agricultural belt

vibe.signatureFeature: A fire-blackened colonnade standing in regrown scrub, with the field boundaries still legible from any rise.
vibe.palette: Charcoal black, bright regrowth green, bleached render.

why.founding: A Khajiit moon-sugar landing on the Murkmire coast — the province gazetteer's only Khajiiti place-name, and it is here for a reason.
why.siteAdvantages: A sheltered landing far enough west of Lilmoth to be outside its tariff and close enough to sell into it.
why.occupantsMotive: Two families left of a dozen; the sugar still lands, in less of it and less often.
why.pressures: Lilmoth's rebuilt council taxes what Moonmarch used to handle untaxed; the trade has moved to Alten Meerhleel.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tariff rise at Lilmoth would refill Moonmarch in a season.

preferences.neighbourRelation: too far inland for its own logistics

vibe.signatureFeature: A Khajiit-built landing of low arcaded warehouses in the wrong climate, three-quarters empty, with the moon-and-crescent still painted over each door.
vibe.palette: Faded ochre and lapis paint, sun-bleached timber, green rot at the base of every wall.

why.founding: A fishing and cockle village on the Topal tidal flat, close enough to Soulrest to sell into it daily.
why.siteAdvantages: Two metres of tide over a firm cockle flat; stilts keep the floors dry and the flat is walkable at low water.
why.occupantsMotive: Sell fresh to the city, sell salted to the coast road, and never owe the council anything.
why.pressures: The city's price is set by buyers who all know each other; the village's answer is to sell early and low.
why.wouldChangeIf: A harbour road extension would turn it into a suburb.

hardConstraints: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed

preferences.neighbourRelation: strung along a waterway, linear not radial

vibe.signatureFeature: A whole village standing on legs over a flat that is water at breakfast and mud at noon, with cockle rakes hung under every floor.
vibe.palette: Grey mud, silver water, reed-brown thatch.
vibe.mood: Busy twice a day, dead between.

why.founding: A kept fire on the road north from Lilmoth, on the stretch where the flood makes the road impassable without warning.
why.siteAdvantages: On the highest point of a four-mile causeway, above every recorded flood.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by the two villages at either end, because both have lost people on this road.
why.pressures: In flood season it holds twenty people for two days at a time and it is built for six.
why.wouldChangeIf: A raised road would empty it permanently.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities

vibe.signatureFeature: A single stone-floored room on a causeway high point, with flood heights and dates cut into its doorpost going back six generations.
vibe.palette: Fire orange, wet stone, brown flood.

why.founding: A seasonal camp on the north-gate road, sited where the road is squeezed between a channel and a rock shoulder.
why.siteAdvantages: A hundred metres of road with no way around it and no sightline until you are in it.
why.occupantsMotive: They call it a toll. Lilmoth calls it robbery. The rate is consistent and negotiated, which supports the former.
why.pressures: Escorted convoys have begun refusing to pay, and nobody has decided yet what happens next.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single killed merchant would turn a tolerated arrangement into a campaign.

hardConstraints: commands traffic and offers an escape

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a route with traffic worth robbing

vibe.signatureFeature: A rope across a road between a channel and a rock, with a fire, a tally stick and four people who are not hiding.
vibe.palette: Rope hemp, wet rock, fire orange.

why.founding: A Naga village on the inner channels that raids the Lilmoth road in the dry season and trades with it in the wet.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep channel water on three sides, one poled approach, and reach to both the road and the estuary.
why.occupantsMotive: Raiding here is seasonal economics, not war; the same households trade with the people they robbed four months earlier.
why.pressures: Lilmoth's council has started paying for road escorts, which changes the arithmetic for the first time in a century.
why.wouldChangeIf: A permanent armed escort would force the village into either full trade or full war.

preferences.neighbourRelation: near the roads its tribeless relatives work

vibe.signatureFeature: A village whose houses face inward onto a single defended water court, with the season's road-take stacked openly in it.
vibe.palette: Dark timber, painted scale-motifs, black water.

why.founding: A village whose whole trade is the dead: staking, tending, reading and repatriating for the whole southern coast.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm peat that holds a stake, central to a dozen villages, and far enough from all of them.
why.occupantsMotive: Every household here holds a grave-office; children learn to read stakes before they learn anything else.
why.pressures: The Owing's dead, Umbriel's dead and White Rose's dead all arrive here eventually, and the ground is filling.
why.wouldChangeIf: A refusal to accept more dead would force a dozen villages to solve the problem themselves.

hardConstraints: soft ground that holds a stake, downwind of everyone

preferences.neighbourRelation: serves 6-12 villages that keep it at arm's length

vibe.signatureFeature: A village surrounded on all sides by standing grave-stakes in ordered ranks, each carved with a whole life and readable by anyone who stops.
vibe.palette: Pale carved wood, peat black, red ochre.

why.founding: A maintained air chamber on the submerged route between the estuary and the inner channels — somebody built the bench in it.
why.siteAdvantages: Halfway along a flooded passage too long to swim in one breath, in a natural dome that holds air.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by the divers who use the route: a bench, a slate, a lamp bracket and a rule about leaving oil.
why.pressures: The air is finite and shared; the slate records who is currently below.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the chamber would close the route to everyone but the very best swimmers.

preferences.neighbourRelation: inside a drowned or flooded place

vibe.signatureFeature: A dry stone bench in a domed air pocket underwater, with a lamp bracket, an oil jar and a chalked list of names currently down.
vibe.palette: Lamp gold on black water, wet grey stone.

why.founding: A mangrove village that grew as a walkway first and a settlement second: the path came, then the houses hung off it.
why.siteAdvantages: A mangrove belt too soft to build on and too dense to boat through, where a raised deck is the only viable form.
why.occupantsMotive: Every household maintains its own span of deck, and the village's shape is the record of who has been diligent.
why.pressures: Three spans are failing and their households have left; the village is branching around the gaps rather than repairing them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A concerted repair would reconnect two halves that are drifting into separate villages.

hardConstraints: crosses water rather than sitting beside it

preferences.neighbourRelation: often the only dry route through its stretch

vibe.signatureFeature: A branching timber walkway through mangrove with houses hung off its sides, and two dead-end spurs that stop at rotten decking.
vibe.palette: Wet dark timber, mangrove green, tannin water.

why.founding: A drowned sinkhole in the bay floor, forty metres deep and occupied by something the fishers will not name at sea.
why.siteAdvantages: The one deep hole in an otherwise shallow bay: cold, dark and permanent.
why.occupantsMotive: The occupant. The fishers work around it in a circle you can see on any chart of their nets.
why.pressures: The hole is directly on the natural lighterage line and every hull crosses it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing anybody here is willing to attempt.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a boat lane, which is the problem

vibe.signatureFeature: A circle of open water that no net is ever set across, with a visible temperature line at its rim and forty metres of black beneath.
vibe.palette: Blue-black, cold green rim, silver bait shoal.

why.founding: The estuary is half a mile wide at the road crossing and the ferry is older than the rebuilt city.
why.siteAdvantages: A narrows with hard landings on both sides and slack water twice a day.
why.occupantsMotive: A council concession, farmed out annually to the highest bidder, which explains the fare.
why.pressures: The fare rises every year and the boats do not improve.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rival free crossing upstream would break the concession and the council's revenue with it.

hardConstraints: across water too deep or wide to ford

preferences.neighbourRelation: a mandatory node in the route graph; has a paired stage

vibe.signatureFeature: A wide flat ferry with a painted fare board that has been repainted over five times, each time higher.
vibe.palette: Painted board red, brown estuary, grey plank.

why.founding: Where the estuary's whole ebb squeezes past a rock spur, running four knots for three hours at a stretch.
why.siteAdvantages: Unavoidable on the river route; the alternative is a day's portage.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives on it. Everyone waits for it.
why.pressures: Loaded canoes are lost here every year and the loss is treated as weather.
why.wouldChangeIf: Cutting the spur back would halve the current and cost more than the province has.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a boat lane; forces a portage or a wait

vibe.signatureFeature: A standing wave off a black rock spur, with a waiting beach on the upstream side worn bare by generations of people sitting out the ebb.
vibe.palette: Brown-white race, black rock, bare mud beach.

why.founding: A reef harvested for lime, lacquer shell and building aggregate rather than for pearl — Lilmoth's stilts need footings.
why.siteAdvantages: Shallow enough to work by free-diving, close enough to barge the take straight to the city.
why.occupantsMotive: Cutters take by permit from the council, which is the only harvest in the bay anyone actually licenses.
why.pressures: The reef is visibly smaller than it was in living memory and the permit count has not fallen.
why.wouldChangeIf: Closing it would raise the cost of every new platform in Lilmoth.

hardConstraints: clear water over a worked bed

preferences.neighbourRelation: worked from a coastal settlement or a flotilla

vibe.signatureFeature: A reef cut into steps like a quarry, with barge moorings over the deepest workings and a permit board on a post.
vibe.palette: Bleached coral white, blue water, grey barge.

why.founding: Two miles of Oliis Bay flat that can be walked at low water and must be sailed at high, and the difference is ninety minutes.
why.siteAdvantages: It cuts four hours off the coast route for anyone who reads the tide correctly.
why.occupantsMotive: Local carriers use it daily; strangers use it once.
why.pressures: The tide comes in across the flat faster than a person walks, from behind.
why.wouldChangeIf: A marked causeway would make it safe and pointless.

hardConstraints: tidal; passable only at low water

preferences.neighbourRelation: a shortcut that halves a journey, on a schedule

vibe.signatureFeature: A two-mile mudflat with withy markers leaning in the direction the flood comes from, and a bell post at each end.
vibe.palette: Silver mud, grey sky, dark withy.

why.founding: A deep-water trader that dragged its anchor in a blow and drove onto the bay flats, where it still stands upright.
why.siteAdvantages: Grounded upright in two metres of water, visible across the whole anchorage.
why.occupantsMotive: Lighter crews use it as a marker and a smoking shelter; the cargo went in the first week.
why.pressures: It is directly on the lighterage line and gets larger in everybody's way every year as it settles.
why.wouldChangeIf: Breaking it up would clear the line and cost more than anyone will pay.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a shipping approach or a hazard

vibe.signatureFeature: A full-rigged trading hull standing upright on a mudflat with its masts still up and washing lines rigged between them.
vibe.palette: Tarred hull black, grey mud, bright washing.
vibe.approach: The one thing in Oliis Bay visible from every direction.

why.founding: Households turned off their ground for owed labour and camped at the edge of it, because leaving would forfeit the claim entirely.
why.siteAdvantages: On the boundary of the estate that evicted them, in sight of their own fields.
why.occupantsMotive: Staying is the claim. Every day here is an argument.
why.pressures: The ledger house says the debt grows while they camp; they say it does not; nobody can read the original entry.
why.wouldChangeIf: Producing the original ledger page would end it one way or the other.

preferences.neighbourRelation: immediately outside an estate village

vibe.signatureFeature: A camp laid out exactly along a field boundary, with the evicted households' door-posts carried from their old houses and re-erected facing the fields.
vibe.palette: Mud, salvaged thatch, green crop beyond.

why.founding: The last rest on the pilgrim route to the Teeth of Sithis, kept by Nisswo of the Turning Path.
why.siteAdvantages: A day short of the temple, on the only firm ground on the final approach.
why.occupantsMotive: They house pilgrims free and preach the decay-sermon at them, which most pilgrims came for.
why.pressures: A rival reading of the sermon is being preached three days back down the route.
why.wouldChangeIf: A schism would split the route and the house with it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: between villages on a preaching circuit

vibe.signatureFeature: A rest house whose walls are deliberately unrepaired, with each year's decay marked and dated as part of the teaching.
vibe.palette: Rotting timber, lamp gold, black water.

why.founding: A xanmeer with no surviving clan, tended instead by the pilgrims who pass it on the way to the Teeth of Sithis.
why.siteAdvantages: On the pilgrim line, with a spring at its foot — the reason the route goes this way at all.
why.occupantsMotive: Maintenance as devotion: each party clears one terrace and moves on.
why.pressures: Pilgrim tending is uneven and sentimental; the terraces nobody likes are being lost.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rerouted pilgrimage would leave it to the forest within thirty years.

preferences.neighbourRelation: a landmark for its whole district; a village within 1 km tends it

vibe.signatureFeature: A stepped monument half swept and half green, with the swept terraces exactly those visible from the path.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, moss green, pilgrim cloth colour.
vibe.approach: Breaks the canopy line from the pilgrim path — one of the few reliable landmarks in Murkmire.

why.founding: Pusbottom's games moved onto the water when the council started raiding buildings, and never moved back.
why.siteAdvantages: Moored outside the wall line, shiftable in an hour, and reachable only by boat.
why.occupantsMotive: Dice, obligation-broking and the buying of debts; the criminal underground of a city that has always had one.
why.pressures: The council knows exactly where it is and moves against it only when a council member loses badly.
why.wouldChangeIf: A licensed gaming house inside the wall would kill it and nobody would propose one.

hardConstraints: a mooring is half the type

preferences.neighbourRelation: in a port, a market town or a slum quarter

vibe.signatureFeature: A lantern-lit barge with a shallow-draught tender always alongside and a bell to warn the tables.
vibe.palette: Lamp red, black water, painted deck.

why.founding: Southern Sea crews — a large share of them Khajiit — keep a low profile to avoid Altmer and Maormer warships, so they anchor where no state looks.
why.siteAdvantages: A deep cove behind a headland with two exits, sand holding ground and a freshwater run at its head.
why.occupantsMotive: Half the hulls here carry a Soulrest charter, and all of them carry cargo the charter does not mention.
why.pressures: Soulrest's council both licenses and disowns them, which is a stable arrangement everyone resents.
why.wouldChangeIf: A Dominion sweep of the Southern Sea would scatter it to the mangroves in a week.

hardConstraints: deep approach, hidden from the lane

preferences.neighbourRelation: near a shipping lane it can reach and leave

vibe.signatureFeature: Six low hulls moored bow-and-stern in a cove, a shore camp of sailcloth, and a chartered ship anchored respectably among them.
vibe.palette: Sailcloth ochre, wet sand, dark cliff green.

why.founding: Canon empties Rockpark of every business and guild through pestilence, plague and a curse; nobody returned because its Hist died.
why.siteAdvantages: Good firm ground on the north-east road out of Lilmoth — which is why its emptiness is so conspicuous.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The Unearthed Equipment Store still blocks the palace gate and the palace still holds what the royal family became.
why.pressures: It is a day's walk from a living city and stocked with two centuries of untouched goods, and still nobody goes in.
why.wouldChangeIf: A confirmed cure for whatever is in the palace would strip the town in a week.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in the country the Flu emptied; other villages avoid it

vibe.signatureFeature: A whole town with its shop shutters closed and its stock still on the shelves, and a collapsed equipment store jammed across the palace gate.
vibe.palette: Dust grey, faded shop-paint, black doorways.
vibe.approach: The road runs straight into it; nothing on the road warns you, which is worse.

why.founding: The reason Rockpark was never resettled: its Hist died, and with it the memory the village kept in it.
why.siteAdvantages: The town's central enclosure, still walled, still swept by pilgrims who come and do not stay.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. Tree-minders from three villages visit annually and take nothing.
