why.pressures: A dead Hist's mnemic egg is a theological emergency nobody in the region wants to be responsible for.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cutting taking root here would change Murkmire's whole map of who is owed what.

preferences.neighbourRelation: beside a bereaved or sap-touched village

vibe.signatureFeature: A hollow grey stump inside a maintained wall, with offerings placed on its rim by people who then leave immediately.
vibe.palette: Ash-grey wood, green wall moss, bright offering cloth.

why.founding: A walkable gallery under a great root mass, dry above the flood, and occupied by people who wanted somewhere no one would look.
why.siteAdvantages: Two hundred metres of natural passage with three entrances and a permanent air flow.
why.occupantsMotive: Whoever is currently in it — the tenancy changes and the fittings do not.
why.pressures: The gallery floods to chest height in the deep wet season, on about a week's notice.
why.wouldChangeIf: A root collapse would close the middle and split it into two dead ends.

hardConstraints: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded

preferences.neighbourRelation: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect, and that connection is the map

vibe.signatureFeature: A living tunnel of root with hearth-scars and shelf niches cut into it at three different heights by three different tenancies.
vibe.palette: Root brown, soot black, green entrance light.

why.founding: The Imperial customs suburb outside Lilmoth's north gate, looted by the An-Xileel when they took the city from the Empire.
why.siteAdvantages: Astride the north road where every cargo had to pass, which is why it was built and why it was sacked.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody rebuilt it; Lilmoth's rebuilt council collects at the quay instead and prefers not to be reminded.
why.pressures: Its record room survived the fire and nobody has read it in two centuries.
why.wouldChangeIf: The records would establish who owned what before 4E 48, which several families would prefer stayed unknown.

hardConstraints: in a port or a city

preferences.neighbourRelation: attached to a living settlement that does not talk about it

vibe.signatureFeature: A burnt street of Imperial offices with the road still running through it, and one vaulted record room with an intact roof.
vibe.palette: Fire-black render, red brick core, green regrowth.

why.founding: Lilmoth's sap trade produced enough people who could not stop that the villages built somewhere to put them.
why.siteAdvantages: Outside the city, upwind, beside running water, with no sap within a day's walk in any direction.
why.occupantsMotive: Run by former users; the treatment is time, water, work and the absence of any supply.
why.pressures: The city's dealers know exactly where it is and one of them funds it, which nobody can decide how to feel about.
why.wouldChangeIf: Closing the illicit taps in the jungle would empty the house in five years.

preferences.neighbourRelation: just outside a settlement, near sap country

vibe.signatureFeature: A long dormitory hall with barred windows facing away from the city, and a work yard of rope-making that never stops.
vibe.palette: Whitewash, rope hemp, running water.

why.founding: A village of the people who pilot Bramman's river, built inside the mangrove wall a mile above its mouth.
why.siteAdvantages: Invisible from the bay; every house sits on the channel it watches; the mangrove is both wall and roof.
why.occupantsMotive: Piloting fees, and a strict internal rule that no two families ever teach the same reach of the river.
why.pressures: Blackguards want the river as a road, Soulrest wants it as a customs problem, and the village wants it to stay a rumour.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the channel were ever charted publicly the village would have no reason to exist.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately not on any lane

vibe.signatureFeature: Platforms cut into the mangrove wall itself, decked between living trunks, with poled canoes hanging in slings above the tide.
vibe.palette: Root black, leaf green, pale lashed cordage.
vibe.approach: You are inside it before you see it.

why.founding: Sealed by its own people when its Hist chamber was emptied, so that whatever remains inside stays inside.
why.siteAdvantages: A low xanmeer on a rise, unremarkable except that its door was closed from within.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing tends it. Its traps are intact and its Hist chamber is not empty in the way the sealers believed.
why.pressures: Two villages disagree about which of them did the sealing, and therefore about who may open it.
why.wouldChangeIf: An agreement between the two villages would open it legitimately for the first time in centuries.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately hard to reach; no village tends it

vibe.signatureFeature: A stone door closed from the inside, with the sealing crew's hand-marks still in the mortar around it.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, ochre mortar, black seam.

why.founding: Closed deliberately by its own people at some point after the Duskfall and never reopened; the mechanisms were left live.
why.siteAdvantages: On a low rise in the burn country, far enough from any village that its closure was a decision, not an abandonment.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing living tends it. The vakka-stone defences still hold charge.
why.pressures: Two treasure crews have gone in this generation and neither came out, which has done more for its security than the traps.
why.wouldChangeIf: A discharge of the vakka stones would open the whole complex at once.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately hard to reach; no village tends it

vibe.signatureFeature: A perfectly fitted stone door with no handle and a discharge-scar fanned across the terrace in front of it.
vibe.palette: Cold grey stone, scorch black, blue-white spark.

why.founding: Where Lilmoth buried the dead of 4E 48 — its own residents, killed first, by their own city's tree and its party.
why.siteAdvantages: Outside the rebuilt wall on the only firm ground large enough, because inside the wall is the mass grave the city stands on.
why.occupantsMotive: A rotating vigil, maintained by the same rule as the tree-minders': never one faction, never one person.
why.pressures: The An-Xileel successor state denies the causation; Lilmoth's whole civic identity depends on it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A reconciliation with the successor state would require abandoning the inscription, and it will not happen.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village

vibe.signatureFeature: A long low wall with names cut into it in three scripts, and a single unnamed section left blank for the ones nobody could count.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, cut-shadow, one green tended tree.

why.founding: Peat is the district's only fuel now the timber is gone, and it is cut on the edge of ground that is already alight underneath.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep dry peat, cuttable in the dry season, close enough to the coast road to sell.
why.occupantsMotive: Cutters work the cool face and race the fire; a cut worked out before the fire arrives is a good year.
why.pressures: The fire moves underground at walking pace and cannot be seen; two cutters were lost last season.
why.wouldChangeIf: Wet-season flooding could quench the whole seam and end both the danger and the fuel.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in the burn country, or supplying a village's fires

vibe.signatureFeature: Stacked drying peats in neat rows with a haze of smoke coming out of the ground fifty paces behind them.
vibe.palette: Chocolate peat brown, blue smoke, scorched orange.

places.name: Soulrest

why.founding: Third-Era provincial capital at the one sheltered deep-water landfall where Topal Bay meets the Southern Sea.
why.siteAdvantages: Peninsula wrapping the bay; a river mouth just south opening a route north-east into the interior; islands screening the approach.
why.occupantsMotive: Four powers hold pieces of it: a merchant council, an orphaned Imperial apparatus, interior tribes, and the river interests who control Bramman's water.
why.pressures: Its gold-and-timber hinterland was burned by the tribes in 3E 427 and never rebuilt; the capital moved; the offices remain, administering nothing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the mines reopened, or if one of the four claimants finally won, the city would stop being a stalemate and start being a capital again.

hardConstraints: bay port at a concealed river's mouth

preferences.neighbourRelation: controls a hidden navigable channel inland
preferences.densityGradient: city core; the province's second densest civil gradient

vibe.signatureFeature: An Imperial administrative shell — palace, courthouse, bonded stores — with an Argonian and Khajiit town grown through and over it, sea-noise stopping dead at the gate.
vibe.palette: Salt-bleached limestone and grey weathered timber under wet green mould; Khajiit awning colour in the dock lanes.
vibe.approach: From the coast road the palace roof reads first; the harbour is only visible past the mole.

places.complexityJustification: A major city: districts, walls, a harbour and four competing authorities. Compiled from the settlement blueprint schema, not hand-placed geometry.

why.founding: Where the Expeditionary Force's transports were cut up for their iron when the Empire stopped paying for them.
why.siteAdvantages: A hard shingle slope inside the mole with deep water at its foot — the only place on the coast a hull can be laid over.
why.occupantsMotive: Breakers who make more from Imperial fastenings than any local trade makes from anything.
why.pressures: The supply of Imperial hulls is finite and nearly finished; the yard has started buying wrecks off the Long Bar and asking nothing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Soulrest ever built ships again, the same slope would serve.

preferences.neighbourRelation: one per major port; the whole coast's hulls come from a handful of these

vibe.signatureFeature: Half a warship's ribcage standing in the shallows, being unmade plank by plank into stacked, sorted, sellable pieces.
vibe.palette: Iron-orange, tar black, sun-silvered oak.

why.founding: Imperial customs bond for gold and timber exports; sealed in 3E 427 when the exports stopped and opened by hand shortly after.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay, behind the harbour office, with its own water gate for lighters.
why.occupantsMotive: Squatters, a bond-clerk's descendant who still keeps the ledger, and whoever needs dry floor space this month.
why.pressures: The ledger records cargo that no longer exists and names families who would rather it did not.
why.wouldChangeIf: A council audit would turn a curiosity into a scandal.

preferences.neighbourRelation: attached to a port or a wharf

vibe.signatureFeature: Imperial iron doors levered off their hinges and stacked neatly inside, as if the theft had been an official act.
vibe.palette: Damp brick, verdigris, ledger-paper cream.

why.founding: A relay post where letters and small freight change from road carriage to poled canoe for the interior river.
why.siteAdvantages: At the river's head of tide, where the coast road first touches navigable water.
why.occupantsMotive: Polers work fixed reaches and hand over; nobody carries a letter more than a day from home.
why.pressures: Letters to the interior are read by three different interests before they arrive and everyone knows it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single through-carrier service would be faster and instantly less trusted.

preferences.neighbourRelation: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay

vibe.signatureFeature: A rack of numbered canoes under a long roof and a board of destination pegs that is the closest thing the district has to a timetable.
vibe.palette: Wet cane, letter cream, river brown.

why.founding: Salvage is one of the three things Soulrest still lives on, and salvage needs a yard to land, sort and sell what comes up.
why.siteAdvantages: On the inner harbour, with a crane frame, a fresh-water rinse and the buyers' benches thirty paces away.
why.occupantsMotive: Diver crews sell by lot; the yard takes a share and asks where nothing came from.
why.pressures: Every lot on the bench is somebody's cargo; the harbour office periodically wants the books.
why.wouldChangeIf: An enforced provenance rule would collapse the trade into the Long Bar's hands.

preferences.neighbourRelation: always paired with drowned ground it works

vibe.signatureFeature: Sorting tables under an open roof, laid out with corroded ironwork, amphora bases and one very good thing per week.
vibe.palette: Rust, salt crust, wet rope.

why.founding: An outside-the-wall fair that runs four times a year because interior traders will not enter Soulrest's gates and the council will not go out.
why.siteAdvantages: Level dry ground beside the coast road, a river landing on one side and the city gate on the other.
why.occupantsMotive: Everyone gets what they want without conceding anything: the tribes do not enter, the council does not leave.
why.pressures: Both sides periodically try to move the fair to their own advantage; it has not moved in eighty years.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the tribes ever entered the city freely, the fair would die and so would the arrangement.

hardConstraints: a landing, because most goods come by water

preferences.neighbourRelation: on neutral ground between settlements, or in an M3+ settlement

vibe.signatureFeature: A permanent grid of empty post-holes and stone stall-bases that fills with tents four times a year and is bare grass the rest of the time.
vibe.palette: Tent ochre and red, trampled green, grey stone bases.

why.founding: Two centuries of Imperial administrators, officers and settlers buried outside Soulrest's wall in consecrated Cyrodilic form.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm dry ground just outside the gate, deliberately not in Argonian burial country.
why.occupantsMotive: Maintained by a single hereditary sexton whose family has outlasted the government that hired it.
why.pressures: Nobody has been buried here in a hundred and forty years and the ground rent has not been paid since.
why.wouldChangeIf: A council decision to build on it would be the moment Soulrest admits the Empire is gone.

preferences.neighbourRelation: attached to a foreign settlement

vibe.signatureFeature: Rows of Nibenese name-slabs sinking at different angles in wet ground, with a swept gravel path kept perfectly clear.
vibe.palette: Grey slab, moss green, raked white gravel.

why.founding: The quayside house where cargo is contracted, crews are hired and the council's tariffs are argued about.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay, between the harbour office and the divers' yard.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper sells information at the same table as beer and considers both a single trade.
why.pressures: Everyone who matters in the port drinks here, which makes it the least private room in the city.
why.wouldChangeIf: A council monopoly on brokerage would empty it.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement

vibe.signatureFeature: One table forty feet long with the day's freight rates chalked on the wall above it in three scripts.
vibe.palette: Beer amber, chalk white, wet-boot grey.

why.founding: Canon states the Synod had no presence within roughly four hundred miles of Lilmoth; this is the nearest station, and it is why.
why.siteAdvantages: Inside Soulrest's wall, on the coast, resuppliable by sea without ever entering the interior.
why.occupantsMotive: A magister and two assistants studying the burn country's ground fires, with a licence that expired long ago.
why.pressures: The council tolerates them for the fees; the interior tribes have made clear how far east they may go.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the sea supply would close the station within a season.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in or near a northern city; rival to the Whispers

vibe.signatureFeature: An Imperial townhouse with an instrument platform on its roof and a permanently lit blue lamp nobody explains.
vibe.palette: Render cream, brass, blue lamplight.

why.founding: An Imperial intelligence office that was never formally closed because the order to close it never arrived.
why.siteAdvantages: An ordinary house in the old administrative quarter with three doors onto three different streets.
why.occupantsMotive: Two clerks, unpaid for a hundred and forty years, still filing reports for a service that no longer exists.
why.pressures: The files are current, comprehensive and worth a great deal to at least four parties.
why.wouldChangeIf: Any of the four getting the files would shift the balance in Soulrest overnight.

hardConstraints: a quiet way out by water

preferences.neighbourRelation: inside a settlement, indistinguishable from it

vibe.signatureFeature: A plain house whose back room holds a complete, up-to-date card index of everyone who matters on this coast.
vibe.palette: Paper cream, lamp brown, ink black.

why.founding: Someone is counting Southern Sea hulls from a headland, and the tally sheets are in Aldmeris.
why.siteAdvantages: A headland with the only clear sightline down the shipping approach, and a boat cove beneath it.
why.occupantsMotive: Three staff, rotated, who buy food in Soulrest and speak excellent Cyrodilic.
why.pressures: Khajiit crews have noticed the pattern of their resupply and are drawing conclusions.
why.wouldChangeIf: Exposure would end it and start something worse.

hardConstraints: overlooks a road, a harbour or a border

preferences.neighbourRelation: watching something that matters; never adjacent to its own side

vibe.signatureFeature: A stone-built 'fisher's hut' on a headland with no nets, no boat and an unobstructed view of forty miles of sea lane.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, gorse yellow, sea haze.

why.founding: Umbriel passed over this village on its way from Lilmoth in 4E 48 and took everyone in it; what stood up afterwards is still standing.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly under the recorded track of the shadow, on ground that was good enough to hold a village and is now avoided entirely.
why.occupantsMotive: The dead here do not leave the village bounds, which is the only reason it is not a regional catastrophe.
why.pressures: It sits between two working villages and forces every journey between them to take an extra half-day.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing it would restore a road that has been broken for a hundred and fifty years.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor, a legible line across the province

vibe.signatureFeature: A village with its doors open, its grave-stakes all pulled and lying, and figures that keep the paths but never cross the boundary ditch.
vibe.palette: Bleached timber, grey figures, sour green ground.
vibe.approach: The boundary ditch is the warning, and it was dug afterwards.

why.founding: A second village on the same track that was emptied and left nothing behind at all — no dead, no damage, no explanation.
why.siteAdvantages: Identical ground to its neighbour, and identically avoided, for entirely different reasons.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Its neighbours will not take its timber even for a hearth.
why.pressures: The absence of any horror here frightens people more than the presence of one next door.
why.wouldChangeIf: A returning family could reoccupy it tomorrow; none has, in a hundred and fifty years.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor, a legible line across the province

vibe.signatureFeature: Sixteen sound houses with their doors standing open and their contents in place, and no bones anywhere.
vibe.palette: Silver-grey timber, green floor growth, flat light.

why.founding: A xanmeer nobody tended after the Burn; the regrowth got into the joints and took it apart over two centuries.
why.siteAdvantages: Its terraces are now the only climbable relief in a flat scrub district.
why.occupantsMotive: A poacher crew uses the upper chamber; the lower ones are full of roots and something else.
why.pressures: Nobody claims it, so nobody defends it, so it is being emptied piece by piece.
why.wouldChangeIf: A clan claiming it would immediately have to defend it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in a district with other xanmeer, showing the range of states

vibe.signatureFeature: A xanmeer being pulled apart by its own vegetation, with root-buttresses standing where the stonework used to be.
vibe.palette: Root grey, stone green, deep leaf shadow.

why.founding: A Khajiit crew's dance barge moored outside the harbour line so that whose jurisdiction it sits in has never been established.
why.siteAdvantages: Moored beyond the mole where the harbour office's authority stops and the council's begins, in the gap between the two.
why.occupantsMotive: Moon sugar, music and card games, none of which are illegal until somebody decides where the barge is.
why.pressures: Every new wharfinger tries to define the mooring; every one gives up.
why.wouldChangeIf: A defined harbour limit would sink the whole business in a night.

hardConstraints: a mooring is half the type

preferences.neighbourRelation: in a port, a market town or a slum quarter

vibe.signatureFeature: A lantern-hung barge with a drum going, moored just far enough out that you have to take a boat to argue with it.
vibe.palette: Lantern gold on black water, silk red.

why.founding: A Khajiit crew took the flat top of a stack as a transfer point because the Southern Sea's smugglers keep a low profile and hate harbours.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep water on all sides, one landable notch, a rock cistern, and no sightline from any inhabited shore.
why.occupantsMotive: Moon-sugar and untaxed cloth change hulls here without either ship entering a port.
why.pressures: Water has to be carried up; the crew is only ever here for days at a time.
why.wouldChangeIf: An Altmer patrol working the Southern Sea would empty it overnight.

preferences.neighbourRelation: the ocean's climbable landmark; visible from the lane

vibe.signatureFeature: A tented platform lashed to the crown of a sea stack with a block-and-tackle hanging over open water.
vibe.palette: Ochre canvas, wet black rock, white spray.

why.founding: An Imperial causeway across the salt marsh, built to carry ore carts and abandoned when the carts stopped.
why.siteAdvantages: The only straight line across four kilometres of marsh, and still the driest one.
why.occupantsMotive: Used by anyone crossing; maintained by nobody.
why.pressures: Three spans are gone; the gaps are swum, waded or jumped depending on the tide.
why.wouldChangeIf: Repairing the spans would restore the fastest route between Soulrest and the burn country.

preferences.neighbourRelation: links two named places directly

vibe.signatureFeature: A stone road running straight out into salt marsh, with three drowned gaps in it that dictate everyone's tide timing.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, salt-marsh olive, tide-line black.

why.founding: A shore hamlet that subsided when the salt pans changed the drainage behind it; the sea came in over a decade.
why.siteAdvantages: It had firm ground once. It does not now, and that is the whole story.
why.occupantsMotive: Empty at low water; the grave-stakes were moved but not all of them.
why.pressures: The pan-holders have never accepted that the pans did it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing brings it back; a second subsidence would take the pans too.

preferences.neighbourRelation: below a living settlement, or beside one that watched it go

vibe.signatureFeature: Roof-ridges and a standing door frame breaking the surface at low tide, with fish in the house floors.
vibe.palette: Grey-green water, black rotted timber, barnacle white.

why.founding: A second Hist in the burn country that an Imperial-era sap concession tapped under licence and never stopped tapping.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands where the licence-holders could reach it by cart, which is exactly why it was chosen.
why.occupantsMotive: The tapping outfit is long gone; the spiles are still in the trunk and somebody is still collecting.
why.pressures: Ashroot's village will not go near it and will not say why in front of outsiders.
why.wouldChangeIf: Pulling the spiles is a two-hour job that nobody has done in a hundred and sixty years.

preferences.neighbourRelation: beside a bereaved or sap-touched village

vibe.signatureFeature: A living Hist with forty iron spiles driven into it in a surveyed grid, each with a numbered ceramic pot beneath.
vibe.palette: Grey bark, iron black, amber sap.

why.founding: Canon: the tribes tolerate Alten Meerhleel because of its Teeba-Enoo court — the ball game is the price the port pays for existing.
why.siteAdvantages: A floored court on the landward margin of the port, where tribal parties can come without entering the trading water.
why.occupantsMotive: The port fields a team and loses politely; the tribes take the result seriously and the trade continues.
why.pressures: A port team that won convincingly would create a diplomatic problem nobody wants.
why.wouldChangeIf: Ending the games would end the tolerance, and the port knows exactly what that costs.

preferences.neighbourRelation: beside an outsider-facing settlement

vibe.signatureFeature: A sunken stone-kerbed ball court beside a trading port, better maintained than any building in it.
vibe.palette: Packed red clay, painted kerb stones, banner cloth.

why.founding: Canon's largest Sithis temple in Murkmire, tended by the Clutch of Nisswo though it no longer serves its original purpose.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep in the marsh at the end of a pilgrim route, with a natural rock formation the temple was built to frame.
why.occupantsMotive: The Clutch maintain it precisely and preach that its loss of purpose is the sermon.
why.pressures: Nobody can now say what the original purpose was, and at least one faction claims to have found out.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rediscovery of the temple's function would split the Clutch.

preferences.neighbourRelation: a regional pilgrimage terminus

vibe.signatureFeature: A colonnade of black stone teeth rising out of standing water, kept scrubbed clean of algae to the waterline and no further.
vibe.palette: Wet black stone, white scrub-line, brown water.
vibe.approach: Visible only from the last bend of the pilgrim water — a deliberate concealment.

why.founding: Canon: in Lilmoth people look to their elders, including retired Shadowscales — and retired Shadowscales trained somewhere.
why.siteAdvantages: An enclosed water-and-root ground an hour outside the city, with three approaches and no sightline into it.
why.occupantsMotive: Two retired scales still keep the ground and still take the occasional sign-born child, which is now illegal in every sense.
why.pressures: The Cheydinhal succession wants the tradition back; Lilmoth's council would rather it did not exist near their walls.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single public execution of a trainee here would force the council to act.

preferences.neighbourRelation: near a hatchery and a major city, deliberately unremarkable

vibe.signatureFeature: A cleared water-ground with weighted posts, blinded approaches and a rack of blunted practice blades kept dry under a root.
vibe.palette: Black water, wet root, dull steel.

why.founding: A shore village on the tidal flat east of Lilmoth, living off what the bay leaves twice a day.
why.siteAdvantages: Two metres of tide over firm flats, with the city's market within a morning's poling.
why.occupantsMotive: Cockles, crabs and salvage; the wrack line is divided between households by a boundary of driven stakes.
why.pressures: Lilmoth's growth means more of everything is bought and less is given; the old sharing customs are visibly lapsing.
why.wouldChangeIf: A bad shellfish year would put half the village into the city's slum quarter.

hardConstraints: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed

preferences.neighbourRelation: strung along a waterway, linear not radial

vibe.signatureFeature: Stake boundaries running straight out across the mudflat from each house, dividing the tide line into private strips.
vibe.palette: Mud silver, weed green, grey stilt timber.

why.founding: The Empire's timber concession: canon's second Soulrest export, felled along a graded haul road to the river.
why.siteAdvantages: A straight graded cut through what was hardwood forest, still the driest walking line in the district.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody works it; the haul road is now the best inland path anyone has.
why.pressures: The forest it cut was the same peat forest that burned; the regrowth is scrub, not timber.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing regrows a hardwood forest in two hundred years.

preferences.neighbourRelation: behind a coastal ex-capital, on a dead haul road

vibe.signatureFeature: A dead-straight overgrown haul road with rotted sleeper timbers still in it, running four miles into scrub.
vibe.palette: Grey deadwood, thorn green, red laterite.

why.founding: A tidal hard where a hull can be hove down and burned clean of Topal Bay's shipworm.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm bottom, four metres of tide range, and a freshwater seep for the boiling coppers.
why.occupantsMotive: Two families who will careen anyone's boat and ask no questions about its last port.
why.pressures: Timber comes from the burn country and is bad; good keel stock now arrives by sea, which is humiliating.
why.wouldChangeIf: Loss of the freshwater seep would move the whole trade a mile east.

preferences.neighbourRelation: serves a port or a water-village cluster

vibe.signatureFeature: Boats lying over on their sides in the mud with fires under them and a smell of pitch you can find from the water.
vibe.palette: Mud grey, pitch black, flame orange.

why.founding: Shellfish beds in the bay's clear inner water, dived since before the Empire and counted since it arrived.
why.siteAdvantages: Five to nine metres of water over a firm shell bottom, sheltered from the Southern Sea swell by the islands.
why.occupantsMotive: Diving families who work in rotation and will fight over a bed's boundary but never over its rest year.
why.pressures: Soulrest buyers set the price; a bed worked out of turn is a feud, not a crime.
why.wouldChangeIf: Warming or a silt pulse off the burn country would kill a bed outright.

hardConstraints: clear water over a worked bed

preferences.neighbourRelation: worked from a coastal settlement or a flotilla

vibe.signatureFeature: Marker withies standing out of open water in a grid nobody on land can read, and a raft of shucking baskets.
vibe.palette: Turquoise shallows, nacre, wet grey shell.

why.founding: Salt is the one export the burning of the mines did not touch, and the bay's shore evaporates well.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide, gently shelving salt-marsh shore with a dry season long enough to crystallise.
why.occupantsMotive: Pan-holders who pay Soulrest a share and sell the rest to fish-curers along the whole south coast.
why.pressures: A wet-season overtop ruins a year; the sea walls are rebuilt by owed labour every spring.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Owing gangs stopped coming, the pans would silt in three years.

hardConstraints: tidal salt water, sun and wind

preferences.neighbourRelation: supplies a whole district's preservation

vibe.signatureFeature: Geometry in a province that has none: rectangles of white crust with black mud walls between them.
vibe.palette: Blinding white, black mud, pale sky.

why.founding: Lilmoth's rule that a second tender is always present when the first listens created a second office, and that office needed a house outside the enclosure.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly outside the Hist enclosure wall, with a door onto it and a door onto the street.
why.occupantsMotive: The rotating second tenders live here in turn; the house belongs to the office, not the person.
why.pressures: The rota is the city's central political institution and every faction has tried to influence it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single tender holding the post permanently would recreate exactly the condition that destroyed the city.

preferences.neighbourRelation: 200-600 m from the village it serves

vibe.signatureFeature: A house with two doors, a duty board listing the next twelve tenders by name, and a bed that is never the same person's for long.
vibe.palette: Pale plaster, duty-board chalk, green tree light.

why.founding: Canon's Tunnel Rats — penal labour worked underground for limited freedom — dug the deep gallery under the gold concession.
why.siteAdvantages: Below the water table, reached by a single incline that the mine office controlled absolutely.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody down there is alive. The bones are Argonian and they never got to the dirt.
why.pressures: Half the gallery is flooded and the rest is on rotten props; the bone-carriers want the dead out and cannot reach them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dewatering effort would turn a grave into a recoverable one — which is the whole point of the bone-carriers' argument.

preferences.neighbourRelation: below or beside a carceral site

vibe.signatureFeature: A timbered incline dropping into standing water, with tally marks cut beside every side-gallery and names cut beside the tallies.
vibe.palette: Black water, wet timber, lamp-yellow.

why.founding: Where the Expeditionary Force met the uprising in the open in 3E 427, on the one piece of ground that suited a legion.
why.siteAdvantages: Flat, firm and treeless — chosen by the Imperials and accepted by the tribes for reasons the tribes have never explained.
why.occupantsMotive: Farmed now. The plough still turns up mail links and the farmers still stack them at the field edge.
why.pressures: Two entirely incompatible accounts of the day are told within a mile of each other.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing. It is a field. That is the disquieting part.

hardConstraints: where an army could deploy — rare here

preferences.neighbourRelation: at a xanmeer, a crossing or a road

vibe.signatureFeature: An ordinary crop field with a cairn of ploughed-up armour fragments growing at its corner, year on year.
vibe.palette: Crop green, rust brown, black soil.

why.founding: An Imperial settler grant of the late Third Era, laid out to Nibenese practice on ground that does not carry stone.
why.siteAdvantages: It looked like firm lowland when it was surveyed in the dry season.
why.occupantsMotive: The fourth generation still farms it, and still refuses to rebuild in reed.
why.pressures: The house has sunk far enough that the ground floor is a cellar; the barn was rebuilt on stilts and nobody discusses the contradiction.
why.wouldChangeIf: One flood year would settle the argument for them.

hardConstraints: tried to be dry and failed

preferences.neighbourRelation: strung along a road at Imperial spacing, not local spacing

vibe.signatureFeature: A stone Nibenese farmhouse standing knee-deep in its own subsidence, beside a perfectly competent Argonian stilt barn.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, green damp line, reed gold.

why.founding: The Imperial villas outside the rebuilt wall sank with their cellars intact, and the cellars are connected.
why.siteAdvantages: A continuous flooded undercroft running two hundred metres, entered from three collapsed floors.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvage crews work the near end under permit; the far end is beyond the permit line and not empty.
why.pressures: The passage is head-height, silt-floored and disorients completely; there is no natural light after the second room.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse at the middle would cut the far cellars off for good.

preferences.neighbourRelation: links two known places by a wet route

vibe.signatureFeature: A flooded Imperial undercroft with mosaic still on the floor under the silt and a guide-rope tied by somebody who did not come back for it.
vibe.palette: Silt brown, mosaic red glimpse, black water.

why.founding: A village that makes vossa-satl and nothing else, and has done for long enough that the craft defines its marriages, its calendar and its politics.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside the one stand of resonant hardwood left in the district, which the village has managed for centuries.
why.occupantsMotive: The instruments sell across the province; the village's real product is the tuning, which cannot be bought elsewhere.
why.pressures: Bright-Throat's chime craft is fashionable and this is not; young makers are leaving for the cliffs.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the hardwood stand would end the craft in a generation.

hardConstraints: landing plus access to its raw material

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a trade water; brokers between neighbours

vibe.signatureFeature: A village where every house has a drying loft of shaped wood and the whole place is tuned each morning, audibly, at once.
vibe.palette: Warm wood, lacquer red, green stand.

why.founding: Households pushed out of Lilmoth's tariff line built against the outside of the city wall, on platforms in the mangrove.
why.siteAdvantages: The wall itself is one side of every house; the mangrove is the other three.
why.occupantsMotive: Close enough to work in the city daily and far enough out to owe it nothing.
why.pressures: The council periodically declares the platforms a fire risk and never removes them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A wall repair programme would demolish the lot without any decision being taken.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately not on any lane

vibe.signatureFeature: Houses built directly onto the outside face of a city wall, with ladders up to a postern the council pretends is sealed.
vibe.palette: Grey wall stone, raw plank, dark water.

why.founding: A wamasu nesting pond; canon has the beast curse all the water around it to deadly convulsions, which makes the pond itself the hazard.
why.siteAdvantages: A still isolated pond with a sand bank the animal returns to, and no through route past it.
why.occupantsMotive: The adult. Egg-poachers come anyway, from downstream, on foot.
why.pressures: The water within thirty metres is lethal while the adult is present, and the adult is usually present.
why.wouldChangeIf: A poached clutch would drive the adult out and free a whole channel network.

hardConstraints: a held pond, still and avoided

preferences.neighbourRelation: a district hazard; villages route around it

vibe.signatureFeature: A pond with a hard sand nest bank, dead fish rimming the edges, and the surface twitching with light before anything is visible.
vibe.palette: Blue-white flicker, black water, pale sand.

why.founding: One of the prisons canon says the Empire built after 1E 2837, sited by the Imperial rule for this province: put it where the marsh is the wall.
why.siteAdvantages: An island of firm ground in burn-country marsh with one causeway, serving the convict-worked mines behind Soulrest.
why.occupantsMotive: Empty of the living. Full of Argonian dead who died away from their Hist and whose bones were never brought to the dirt.
why.pressures: The Blackrose Chainbreakers want the dead repatriated; the structure is sound enough that somebody will eventually want it back.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reoccupation by any armed party would make the repatriation impossible and the grievance permanent.

preferences.neighbourRelation: far from everything, by design

vibe.signatureFeature: A white lime-rendered Imperial block, structurally perfect and utterly silent, standing above marsh with its causeway intact and its gate open.
vibe.palette: Lime white, marsh brown, black door-shadow.
vibe.approach: It reads white through the reeds from a long way off — one of the few real long sightlines in the lowland.

why.founding: The bar that made the salvage economy: a coral and shell reef lying a foot under at high water across the bay mouth.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly on the natural sailing line into Topal Bay, which is exactly the problem.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing lives here but the reef; three centuries of hulls do.
why.pressures: Silt from the burn-country rivers is killing the living head and turning it to rubble, which makes it more dangerous, not less.
why.wouldChangeIf: A lit mark on the headland would render it merely scenery.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a shipping approach; explains the wrecks and the lights around it

vibe.signatureFeature: A white line of breaking water with mast-stumps standing out of it at intervals, like a fence.
vibe.palette: White surf, dead coral grey, deep blue beyond.

why.founding: The Umbriel Witness Society keeps a standing camp on the shadow track, on the principle that the province is not clean until every stripped place is accounted for.
why.siteAdvantages: On the track itself, between two stripped villages, deliberately in the worst possible place.
why.occupantsMotive: They record, they count, they refuse to leave. Nobody has asked them to.
why.pressures: The society is old, small and increasingly composed of people who were not born when it started.
why.wouldChangeIf: Completion of the survey would dissolve the society, which several members plainly dread.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor

vibe.signatureFeature: A permanent camp of survey tents with a boarded map of the shadow track under a canvas awning, updated in three different hands.
vibe.palette: Canvas grey, ink black, sour green.

why.founding: A Sithite work-and-unmake ground where the local xanmeer carvings of the extinct wraxu are copied in clay and destroyed each year.
why.siteAdvantages: A sheltered clay bank under a xanmeer face that carries the original wraxu etchings canon records here.
why.occupantsMotive: Nisswo and their students make an exact copy of the frieze, exhibit it for one night, and break it before dawn.
why.pressures: Outsiders keep trying to buy the copy; the Clutch keeps having to explain that the destruction is the work.
why.wouldChangeIf: A copy surviving a year would be a theological crisis, and someone is trying to arrange one.

preferences.neighbourRelation: near a Nisswo circuit

vibe.signatureFeature: A stone frieze of extinct birds above a clay bank littered with the broken shards of every copy ever made of it.
vibe.palette: Ochre clay, grey stone, feather-black shard.

why.founding: Named for the extinct wraxu birds whose colonies canon puts on this coast; the birds that nest here now are not them.
why.siteAdvantages: Vertical sea stacks off the islands, unclimbable from three sides, thick with guano and eggs.
why.occupantsMotive: Egg-takers come twice a year by rope and take the ledges in a fixed order.
why.pressures: Everyone here knows what happened to the wraxu, and the taking rules are stricter than any law Soulrest ever wrote.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single greedy season would be remembered for a century.

preferences.neighbourRelation: the ocean's climbable landmark; visible from the lane

vibe.signatureFeature: Two pale stacks streaked white, loud enough to hear from a mile out, with old rope anchors still driven into the rock.
vibe.palette: Guano white, black basalt, green sea.

why.founding: Canon records local xanmeers etched with the extinct wraxu birds; this is the one the coastal clans still maintain as a monument.
why.siteAdvantages: A stepped stone mass on firm ground above the flood, visible above the canopy — one of the district's few true landmarks.
why.occupantsMotive: A clan rota clears the terraces, re-cuts the etchings and forbids entry; looting here is a serious offence and they will say so.
why.pressures: Antiquarians want inside; the Soulrest council has been asked to compel access twice.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single sanctioned excavation would end the tending and probably the clan's standing.

preferences.neighbourRelation: a landmark for its whole district; a village within 1 km tends it

vibe.signatureFeature: Clean-swept stone terraces with bird figures cut deep into every riser, and a sealed doorway that is dusted daily.
vibe.palette: Grey-green stone, cut-line shadow, swept sand.
vibe.approach: The stepped mass breaks the canopy line long before you reach it.

why.founding: A xanmeer's original water shaft, now the only way into a complex whose surface entrances were sealed.
why.siteAdvantages: A vertical stone shaft dropping eleven metres to a flooded gallery, with a ledge at four metres to rest on.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Two ropes hang in it from different decades.
why.pressures: One breath down, one breath back, and the gallery below has its own current.
why.wouldChangeIf: A silt slump would close it and seal the complex entirely.

preferences.neighbourRelation: the only entrance to a submerged place

vibe.signatureFeature: A perfectly circular cut stone shaft full of clear water, with carved handholds spiralling down its inside face.
vibe.palette: Clear blue-black, cut stone grey, green rim growth.

why.founding: Canon's sunken shrine to Xhon-Mehl the Fisher, Ancestral Organ Lord of Lilmoth — the city's own drowned ancestor-god of the catch.
why.siteAdvantages: In the estuary shallows off the old waterfront, submerged by the same subsidence that took the Imperial quarter.
why.occupantsMotive: Fishers dive to it before a long season and leave an offering inside rather than on it.
why.pressures: The city's council would rather the shrine were on land and administrable; the fishers prefer it exactly where it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: Raising it would be an act of civic policy and a religious insult in the same gesture.

preferences.neighbourRelation: between a village and a lair

why.founding: Canon's ancient calendar in the lowlands east of Lilmoth, with a hereditary keeper — a jekka-wass — and a function: it is called a catalyst of change and can alter the weather.
why.siteAdvantages: An open lowland with a clean southern horizon, because the instrument needs one.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper's whole office is not to use it, and to explain that to everyone who arrives wanting it used.
why.pressures: Every party with a weather problem eventually comes here; the keeper has refused emperors' agents and antiquarians alike.
why.wouldChangeIf: A successful use would be the largest single event in the province's recent history, which is the argument for and against.
